actor_pool:
Actor pool infrastructure — slot allocation, linked-list management and state copying (Bank $00, 11 routines).

ActorPoolAllocator (JSL; needs D = 0 because it reads the DP pointer ($4E)) pops the next free slot from a LIFO free list of slot addresses. The list lives in page $0E (InitActorPool builds it at $0E00, 84 entries of $30-byte slots from $1000). Carry clear + Y = new slot base ($1000 + index×$30), or carry set + Y = $1FC0 when exhausted (a negative entry marks the end). It increments activeActorCount.

AllocateActorBefore/After allocate with D temporarily 0, splice the new slot into the doubly-linked actor list ($04 = prev, $06 = next, head/tail in $56/$58) before or after the current actor (X = D = current), then call CopyActorState. UnlinkActor removes the actor at X from the list and calls ReturnActorSlot, which pushes the slot back on the free list and decrements the counters. It must be entered with D = X (the actor being freed); Die, MarkDeath, KillPrev and KillNext all arrange that.

CopyActorState (spawner X = D, new actor Y) copies $0E, $10, $12, the X/Y position, animation index and frame counter, the spriteset/metasprite/stats pointers and the spriteset bank. It forces $2000 on in $10 and clears $0803 there, clears $1000 in $12 (the display-filter flag), and stores the spawner's slot in $0024 (OQ-65). It zeroes parentId, the $2C/$2E movement chain pointers, moveScratch1/2, the $08 timer and chatPtr, and, except in scene $FF (inventory), also extendedFlags and the callback fields.

MarkChildActor sets the new actor's parentId to the spawner's parentId, or to the spawner's own slot if it has none. SetActorBody applies the current characterForm's body_table entry (6 bytes per form) to the actor's spriteset pointer and bank and clears playerFlags bit $8000 (sprite override). AnimFrameLookup returns the word at move_chain_table[A×2], the head pointer of a movement delta chain; its callers are the force-move COP handlers. AllocateSpecialActor appends a slot from the thinker pool to the thinker list (tail in $5C). PaletteResetAndKillThinker is a thinker script body: COP PaletteRestart, PaletteStep, KillThinker.
ambient_palette_cycler:
Generic ambient palette animation thinker (Bank 00): 59 spawn entries in the scene spawn lists of tables/scene_thinkers.

The script is an endless loop of two COP ops. PaletteRestart (re)starts the palette bundle whose ID is already in animScratch+2; for a thinker that value is the spawn parameter byte, so nothing is hardcoded here. PaletteStep then plays the bundle: its entry point stays on that op and it yields until the last strip frame has been shown, after which execution falls through to the BRA and the whole bundle starts again. One six-byte routine therefore repeats any palette bundle forever, and a scene attaches several instances with different bundle IDs to animate independent colour ranges at once. The thinker has no flag gating and no exit of its own; it lives as long as the scene's thinkers.

Examples (bundles decoded from palette_bundles): bundle $30 (scenes 21-23) is six one-frame strips (wait value 5 each) that each rewrite a six-colour ramp starting at CGRAM colour $72, rotated by one colour per strip, i.e. a colour rotation; bundle $13 (scenes 1D and 27) is four frames of a 16-colour palette starting at colour $C0 with wait value 9 per frame. The bundle-ID list per scene is in scene_thinkers; what each bundle looks like on screen was not traced for all of them. The earlier "torch flicker, water shimmer, sky gradient" list was a guess.

ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef:
Orbit placement helper (Bank 00, 62409-62503). It sets the calling actor's position to a base point plus a circular offset: X += sin(angle) * r, Y += cos(angle) * r with r = diameter / 2. Two entries:
- ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef: Y = a reference actor (slot address). Copies that actor's pixel X / Y ($0014 / $0016) into the caller's $14 / $16 first, then falls into the second entry.
- ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef_AddToCurrent: skips the copy and ADDS the offset to whatever $14 / $16 already hold, so the caller must have written the centre there (otherwise the offset accumulates). It is entered from 5 sites (mtA1_fire_sprite 2, attack_ability_system, pyDD_queen_spirit_attack, unused_mode7_boss).

Inputs: X = the caller's actor slot, D = X (the DP $14 / $16 are the caller's), 16-bit A. orbitAngle ($7F0010,X) is read as a BYTE: 256 steps per turn, 1.40625 degrees each. orbitDiameter ($7F0012,X) is also read as a byte, so a diameter above 255 is not possible. The routine clobbers A, Y and the flags, keeps X and D, and returns with A 16-bit.

Arithmetic: for each axis the table value (sine_table_8bit for X, signed_cosine_table_8bit for Y, both indexed by the angle byte; the sine table is only a quarter wave and entries 64-255 read on into the cosine table) is turned into a magnitude, the sign is kept in the carry flag, the magnitude times the diameter is formed with Multiply8x8Unsigned (which preserves carry and Y), the high byte of the 16-bit product is taken (>> 8) and negated when the carry says so. The table peak is $7F, so each offset is about +/- diameter / 2 (the name 'diameter' is right: it is the full width of the circle). Angle 0 puts the actor directly BELOW the centre (cosine peak, Y grows downward); $40 is east, $80 north, $C0 west, so increasing angles turn counter-clockwise on screen.

Callers: 21 JSL sites in 11 files: attack_ability_system 2, btE4_kara, ec0E_lily, ir29_castoth, mtA1_fire_sprite 5, pyDD_queen_orb_shot, pyDD_queen_spirit_attack, cop_handlers_effects (SpiralStep, with the reference actor in $0000), item_use_system, statue_inventory_reward and unused_mode7_boss 6. 16 use the first entry and 5 the second. The elliptical variant with separate X / Y angles is ApplyOrbitalOffsetXY.

The old header said 'multiplied by orbitDiameter ... result updates actor $14/$16' without the sign, byte-width and rotation direction facts above. UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (read from the code and the table headers).
ApplyOrbitalOffsetXY:
Elliptical orbit offset (Bank 00, 62514-62606). It ADDS an offset to the actor's own position ($14 / $16), computed from two independent angle / diameter pairs in the actor's extended WRAM page, so the caller must first write the orbit centre into $14 / $16 before every call (otherwise the offset accumulates). gw8A_sand_fanger reloads the centre from moveXAlt / moveYAlt, awB1_goldcap from its own WRAM fields.

Fields, one byte each, indexed by X = actor slot ($7F0010 + X ...): +0 X angle, +1 Y angle, +2 X diameter, +3 Y diameter. orbitAngle and orbitDiameter are the word views of the two pairs (low byte = X, high byte = Y). One angle step is 1.40625 degrees (256 per turn).

X offset = (|sine_table_8bit[angleX]| x diameterX) >> 8 with the sign of the table value; Y offset = the same with signed_cosine_table_8bit[angleY] and diameterY. The table peak is $7F, so each offset is about +/- diameter / 2 and the diameter is the full width of the ellipse. With equal angles the point starts below the centre (sine 0, cosine at its peak, Y grows downward) and moves right, then up, then left: counter-clockwise on screen. Different angle rates give Lissajous paths.

The sign travels in the carry flag from the table lookup through Multiply8x8Unsigned, which preserves carry. The routine clobbers A, Y and the flags; X (the actor slot) and D are preserved. It ends with A and the index registers 16-bit.

Callers (3 sites): gw8A_sand_fanger (2) and awB1_goldcap (1, where the X diameter grows by 3 and the Y diameter by 2 per step so the path spirals outward). The old header also listed statue_inventory_reward, which uses ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef instead.
ApplyPlayerHitstun:
Player damage and knockback entry (Bank 00, 50071-50198), called by JSL from enemy attack scripts. Registers: A = damage with bit 15 as a 'heavy hit' flag, Y = knockback direction code (0 south, 1 north, 2 west, 3 east, 4 or more = none). The old header said 'damage in Y and knockback metadata on the stack' and that damage is halved; neither is true.

=== STEPS ===

1. $0000 := Y (absolute scratch, kept for later) and $0002 := 0. ASL moves bit 15 of A into carry: when set, $0002 := $FFC4 (the heavy-hit counter). LSR restores the damage with bit 15 cleared; it is NOT halved (ASL then LSR cancel out).
2. playerHp := max(0, playerHp - damage). D and X become the player actor.
3. Player flags $10 |= $0080 (hit reaction); the iframe counter ($7F0028) := $0002 if nonzero, else $003C. A positive counter is hit-stun, a negative one is recovery / invincibility (see actor_execution).
4. If playerFlags bit $0800 (script / ability lock) is set, no stagger is spawned: only the D-pad bits $0F00 of joypadMaskStd are cleared. Otherwise HitStaggerMain is spawned with COP SpawnListAppend ( entry, 0, 0, #$2400 ): $2400 is the child's FLAGS word ($2000 script-driven, $0400 player victim), not a priority as the old header says. Y = the child slot afterwards.
5. Y = $1FC0 means the actor pool was full and the spawn failed: the D-pad bits $0F00 are cleared (some callers hide them first; the child that would have restored them does not exist). The code still falls through to the child-setup stores below with Y = $1FC0, unlike ApplyInteractionDamage, which skips them (OQ-I046-2).
6. Child setup: extendedFlags bit $0020 of the player is copied to the child, the direction code from $0000 goes into the child's $28, and its $2C / $2E are zeroed. Hit sound: PlaySoundCh2 #07 (always the Will sound; combat_collision picks #08 for Freedan and Shadow).

The function never HIDES the D-pad (the old header said it masks joypad input 'for heavy hits or when the climbing flag is active'): it only reveals it on the two no-stagger paths. Callers such as gw82_archer and ir1F_stone_guard hide it themselves (TSB #$0F00) before the JSL, and HitStaggerReleasePlayer reveals it when the stagger ends.

Because HitStaggerReleasePlayer overwrites the iframe counter with $FFE2 when the slide ends, the $003C written here only lasts until then (about 17 ticks).

=== CALL SITES (9, in 3 files) ===

| File | A | Y |
|------|---|---|
| gw82_archer (2 sites) | 2, 2 | 3 (east), 2 (west) |
| gw83_asp (3 sites) | 1, 1, $8001 (heavy) | 4, 4, 4 (no knockback) |
| ir1F_stone_guard (4 sites) | $0B02 + 2, $0B02 + 2, 2, 2 | 0, 1, 3, 2 |

$0B02 is the difficulty level (ram_map.txt), so the stone guard's two strongest hits add it to a base of 2. The old docs say about 12 callers; there are 9. Combat hits from the player's own attacks and from contact use combat_collision's inline code instead.

boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0:
Enix logo palette thinker for OBJ palette 0 (Bank 00, 47167-47186). The palette cycle of the Enix logo is run by three thinkers, one per OBJ palette: this one (OBJ palette 0, CGRAM colours $81-$8F, bundles $50 / $52 / $54), boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1 (OBJ palette 1, $91-$9F, bundles $51 / $53 / $55) and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2 (OBJ palette 2, $A1-$AF, bundles $56 / $57 / $58). Scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 0, param #01) spawns all three together. They start with the scene and run side by side, in BOTH visits of scene $FB (sFB_boot_logo reloads the scene for the second logo), so each visit animates OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2 at once. Only the second logo, the Enix logo (sprite_group_000010 in spm_boot_logos), uses those palettes, so only it changes colour; the first logo is on OBJ palette 3, which no thinker touches, so in the first visit these thinkers run unseen.

This thinker plays palette bundles $50, $52 and $54 in order: PaletteStart selects a bundle and PaletteStep runs it to its end (the op continues only when the bundle is finished), three times, then KillThinker. The param byte #01 is never read (PaletteStart overwrites animScratch+2 with the bundle ID). Header word $0800: bit 11 keeps it running in the lighter frame routines, bit 2 is clear (runs before the actors).

=== THE BUNDLES (palette_bundles, bank $16) ===

Each bundle has 8 sub-entries of one frame each. A frame is 15 colors (30 bytes) written to CGRAM colors $81 to $8F, i.e. colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 0 (boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1 writes $91 to $9F, OBJ palette 1, and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2 $A1 to $AF, OBJ palette 2). There is 1 extra tick between frames in $50 and $52 and 3 in $54.
$50 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_reveal): starts all black; a 13-color ramp from dark purple ($2C4B) to white ($7FFF) grows across colors 1 to 13, its white tip moving from color 1 to color 13 with the darker colors trailing it; colors 14 and 15 stay 0.
$52 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_whiten): the ramp turns white from its bright end towards its dark end until all 13 colors are white, while colors 14 and 15 brighten from $18C6 / $2108 to $4E73 / $6739.
$54 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_settle): starts all white and fades back down to the ramp (steps through $777D, $6AFA, ... to $2C4B ... $7FFF) while colors 14 and 15 darken to $1425 / $2449.
So the logo's palette sweeps in, flashes to white and settles on a rainbow ramp: a shine effect. This is read from the colour values (not run).

=== WHERE THE COLOURS LAND ===

In sprite_group_000010 (the second logo, spm_boot_logos) OBJ palette 0 colours 8 of the 16 parts of the 4 x 4 emblem block (parts $05 to $0A, $0E, $0F: the lower two rows), OBJ palette 1 the other 8 (parts $00 to $04, $0B to $0D: the upper two rows). Both get the same shine at the same time, so the emblem sweeps in, flashes white and settles.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The three thinkers were first called boot_logo_palette_enix, boot_logo_palette_quintet and boot_logo_palette_third. Those were spawn-order names and read like three companies or three steps; they are one palette cycle, the Enix logo's, split over OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2 (the old header's 'animates the Enix logo colors' was right for all three). The old header called this the first of three thinkers and the Quintet note said it runs 'after the Enix palette sequence'; they are spawned together and run in parallel. The logo is the second logo of scene $FB, the 4 x 4 emblem with a wordmark under it; I054 left the question of which logo uses OBJ palettes 0 and 1 open (OQ-I054-1) and the sprite tables answer it.

boss_clear_reward_handler:
Post-boss stat catch-up actor (Bank 00, 49854-50070), spawned from scene_actors in the five boss arenas (Castoth, Viper, the Mu vampires, Sand Fanger, the Mummy Queen). Once the boss is dead it grants, in one go, the stat reward of every room of that dungeon whose clear reward the player has not yet taken.

=== FLOW ===

1. BossRewardCheckInit: find sceneCurrent in boss_reward_range_table (4-byte rows: scene, first scene, last scene, pad; the first match wins). The row's byte offset is kept in $20, offset / 4 is the boss number. If wramFlags $0100 + boss number (event flags $0500-$0507) is already set the actor only idles.
2. Every frame (SetEntryHere): wait for playerFlags bit $0020 (boss defeated). Then BossClearApplyStatReward walks enemy_clear_reward_table over the scenes [first, last): each scene with a nonzero tier whose scene flag $0300 + scene is clear gets the flag set and its stat raised (1 = Max HP, 2 = STR, 3 = DEF, +1 each). It is the same flag that the per-room clear reward (reward_actors, field_reveal_object) tests, so a room cannot pay twice.
3. hpToHeal := maxHp - hp (UpdateHUD refills the bar at 1 HP per 8 frames, which also covers the extra max HP), the boss flag is set, and the actor idles for the rest of the scene.

=== QUIRKS ===

- The scene search has no end-of-table test; it relies on the actor existing only in the five boss arenas. Rows 5-10 are placeholders (scene $F8 and $29 with an empty range); the first $29 row is the real one.
- The range end is compared only after a zero tier. In the shipped table the entry at the end index (the boss scene itself) is zero in all five ranges, which ends the walk, so a nonzero run past the end cannot happen.
- The entry stores the range word in the actor's $04 and the apply routine uses $04 and $0E as scratch. wram-memory-map lists $04 as prevActorLink (the actor list predecessor): OQ-I051-3.
- The old header called the HP effect a 'damage-flash timer'; $0B22 is the heal counter hpToHeal. The old routine comment said the flags are per enemy; the index is the scene id.
camera_drift:
Camera drift library (Bank 00, 53134-53350): three short-lived actor scripts that nudge the camera during set pieces. Scene scripts spawn them with SpawnAfterFlags / SpawnListAppend; each dies when finished.

=== CALLERS ===

CameraDriftLoopSimple: pyCD_flame_statue, ir25_ceiling_tile, ir29_castoth. CameraDriftLoopShip: st68_kara (Angel Village undersea tunnel), gs2D_lily, gs2D_lance, gs2B_erik (Gold Ship). CameraDriftPatterned: awB1_gorgon, pyD9_dangerslide_controller, ir29_castoth (3 sites).

=== VARIABLES ===

cameraTargetX / Y ($06BE / $06C2) are the layer-0 scroll targets (camera_scroll_controller recomputes them each frame). cameraDeltaX / Y ($06C0 / $06C4) are the layer-1 (second background layer) scroll POSITION, not per-frame deltas: the layer1_scroll_actors actors and camera_scroll write them, and CameraSmoothScroll copies them to effectScrollH / V ($068C / $0690, the BG2 scroll) when layerPriorityFlag bit $0400 is set. While that mode is active the drift therefore moves both layers together. These are not the effectDeltaX / Y ($06E4 / $06E6) that camera_scroll_controller writes. Whether the offsets added here survive the recompute is not established statically (OQ-I050-2).

=== CameraDriftLoopSimple ===

LoopStart #$78 runs 120 passes, one frame each (every LoopEnd pass yields). Each pass adds r = (RngByte and 3) - 1, that is -1, 0, +1 or +2 (bias +0.5), to cameraTargetY and to cameraDeltaY. Nothing is undone at the end. The same formula is the Y shake in player_character. Then Die. The old note said 'random +-1'.

=== CameraDriftLoopShip ===

Sets $12 bit $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, so the drift also runs in the display-filtered modes) and $26 := 0 ($26 = the offset applied last frame). 120 passes: while playerFlags bit $0100 (forced walk) is set a pass does nothing; otherwise cameraDeltaY -= $26 (undo last frame), $26 := RngByte and 3 (0 to 3), then cameraTargetY += $26 and cameraDeltaY += $26. After the loop it yields once (SetEntryHereAndYield), subtracts the last $26 from cameraDeltaY and dies. So the delta offset is temporary (each frame replaces the previous one) while the target offset is not undone here.

=== CameraDriftPatterned ===

$28 := RngByte (random starting phase), $2A := 2, SetEntryHere. Each run: DBR := program bank (to read camera_drift_offsets), Y offset := table[$28 and 7] then $28++, added to cameraTargetY (a negative result is clamped to 0) and, unless $24 = $FFFF, to cameraDeltaY (clamped to 0); then the X offset := table[$28 and 7], i.e. the next entry, with the same rules. A run is followed by $08 := 3 (the next run starts 4 ticks later) and DEC $2A; the third run ends in Die, so the runs fall 4 ticks apart (the third 8 ticks after the first) and the actor applies 3 Y and 3 X offsets before it dies. The next run's Y entry is the previous run's X entry.
camera_drift_offsets holds 16 words but the index is masked to 3 bits, so only the first 8 are used: +1, -1, -2, +1, +2, 0, -2, +1 (sum 0). The last 8 words (+5, -4, -2, +4, +1, -5, +4, -3, also summing to 0) are never read.
camera_scroll:
Camera scroll actor definitions and shared subroutines (Bank 00).

Defines four actor-based camera scroll behaviors used during gameplay and cutscenes. Each actor sets bit 12 ($1000) of its status word ($12; the meaning of that bit was not verified) and then computes per-frame scroll deltas with the hardware multiply/divide unit (MulDivide).

Spawn parameters: the X/Y bytes of the actor-spawn entry are not positions. The spawner makes them pixel coordinates (tile × 16); TileAlignCoord then packs each into (page << 8 | tile) and ComputeScrollDeltas passes it to MulDivide as the packed operand: low byte = multiplier, high byte = divisor. Zero skips the axis. Spawn bytes seen in extracted/: #11 (most common), #21, #41, #00, #DF (Init only). The −8 px X offset makes the X multiplier one less than the Y one for the same spawn byte (OQ-57).

The four scroll modes are:
- ScrollCameraInit: aligns both coordinates, runs the delta computation 3 times (identical inputs), copies the Y delta to effectScrollV, then computes once more and moves cameraDeltaX (bit 15 set) into forcedScrollOverride, zeroing cameraDeltaX. Used only with spawn #DF, #DF.
- ScrollCameraTrack: aligns once, then recomputes both deltas every frame.
- ScrollCameraVertical: aligns once, then recomputes only the Y delta every frame (X ignored).
- ScrollCameraAccumulate: recomputes both deltas every frame and adds the accumulators in DP $24/$26 (zeroed at start, writable by other actors).

Shared subroutines:
- TileAlignCoord: packs a pixel coordinate into (page << 8 | tile): LSR ×4 in 8-bit mode shifts only the low byte, the high byte is kept, then AND #$0F0F. Result in Y.
- TileAlignPosition: applies TileAlignCoord to X ($14, after subtracting 8) and Y ($16).
- ComputeScrollDeltas: for each axis, MulDivide(A = packed ratio from $14/$16, Y = cameraTargetX/Y) → cameraDeltaX/Y; an axis whose packed value is 0 is skipped and keeps its previous delta.
camera_scroll_controller:
Per-frame camera tracking actor (Bank 00, 60144-60314), the camera actor of 220+ field scenes. It reads the player's position, derives the scroll position that centres the player (clamped to the scene's window) and publishes the distance from the current scroll to that target as effectDeltaX / effectDeltaY for the layer1_scroll_actors actors (Layer1DriftUnbounded, Layer1DriftWrapped, Layer1ParallaxRatio). It scrolls nothing itself.

=== ENTRY AND FREEZE ===

actor-def: sprite 0, flags 0, header byte $2C. Every run sets $12 bit $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier that lets the actor run in the display-filtered and overlay-only modes; CopyActorState never copies it), calls SetEntryHere and returns at once when layerPriorityFlag bit $0200 is set (camera frozen; the attack setup in player_character sets it).

=== PLAYER POSITION ===

D := playerActorDp (the player's actor slot), so $14 / $16 are the player's pixel X / Y. playerXPos := X - 8 and playerYPos := Y - $10 (sprite-adjusted reference point), playerXTile / playerYTile := those values >> 4. These four words are refreshed every frame, also while the target is held.

=== TARGET (skipped while playerFlags bit $0100, forced walk, is set) ===

Per axis, with P = the player actor's pixel position (not the adjusted one): t = P - $80. If t is negative or below cameraOffset, the target is cameraOffset (left / top limit). Otherwise e = t + $100; if e is at or beyond cameraBounds the target is cameraBounds - $100, else it is t. So cameraOffset is the left / top edge of the scene's window and cameraBounds the right / bottom edge. There is no dead zone: the old note called the P - 128 centring a 'dead zone'.
Both axes use the constants $80 and $100. Horizontally that centres the player in the 256-pixel view; vertically the target puts the player 128 lines below the top of a 224-line screen, 16 lines below the middle (OQ-I049-4). The result goes to cameraTargetX / cameraTargetY.

=== DELTAS ===

effectDeltaX := cameraTargetX - bg1ScrollH and effectDeltaY := cameraTargetY - mapScrollV ($068E, the vertical scroll that UploadScrollRegisters writes to BG1VOFS; the old comment said BG2). This also runs while the forced walk holds the target, so the deltas keep following whatever forced_walk wrote to the target.

=== DEAD CODE ===

CameraDeadBoundsX and CameraDeadBoundsY (LDA cameraBoundsX / cameraBoundsY, BRA) are never branched to: the preceding code ends in BRA, and no other file references them.

cop_dispatch:
Central COP bytecode dispatch engine for IOG's actor and thinker scripting system (Bank $00).

CopDispatch is a 24-byte native-mode entry reached from the COP interrupt vector (CopVector → JML CopDispatch). The byte after the COP opcode ($02) is the handler opcode (the pushed PC − 1). The dispatcher caches the bank in $0C and the operand pointer in $0A, doubles the opcode and jumps through cop_dispatch_table.

The table has 227 word entries: 209 valid opcodes ($00–$6D and $80–$E2) pointing at short-address handler labels, and an 18-entry gap of #$0000 for $6E–$7F that would jump to address 0 (RAM) if executed. cop_table_sentinel follows the table; it is not a real guard (see its note). All 209 table ids match db-us/copdef.json ids, but 19 handler labels differ from the script-side copdef names (listed in the table note).

Every actor and thinker script routes through this dispatcher. Handlers receive the actor slot in X and Y (and D), DBR = $81 and the operand pointer in $0A. They exit with RTI (continue or branch, new PC stored at $02,S) or RTL after popping the COP frame (yield or halt).

Dispatch targets: the 30 cop_handlers_* blocks included below. Support blocks called by handlers but not dispatch targets: actor_pool and flag_helpers.
cop_handlers_actor_death:
Actor-death COP handlers (Bank $00): MarkDeath (#A7), Die (#E0), KillPrev (#A8) and KillNext (#A9).

All of them remove an actor from the doubly linked actor list ($04 = prev, $06 = next, list ends in $0056/$0058) through actor_pool.UnlinkActor, which also returns the slot to the free list. MarkDeath and Die first test $12 bit $0040 ("this actor has marked children", set by the Marked spawn COPs): when it is set they take the shared cascade at UnlinkChildrenCascade, which removes the actor together with every adjacent actor whose parentId ($7F001C) equals its slot address. MarkDeath then resumes the script (RTI through MarkDeathResumeHandler); Die ends it (RTL).

KillPrev and KillNext switch context to the neighbouring actor ($04 / $06) and unlink that actor instead. Neither checks for a null link, so the neighbour must exist.
cop_handlers_actor_flags:
Two collision-layer branch COP handlers (39658–39817, Bank 00).

Despite the block name (cop_handlers_actor_flags), these are collision probes, not flag setters: both sample the collision layer at the actor's tile and branch on the result (7 script sites between them, in gw82_archer, gw82_eyesore and dm_follower_behavior).
- BranchIfBehindWall (COP #5D): branch when the tile occludes the actor (blocked, out of bounds, or an odd type); fall through (skip the operand) when the actor is visible.
- BranchIfCollisionTypeEq (COP #62): branch when the tile's low nibble EQUALS the operand or the position is out of bounds, despite the "Ne" (not-equal) in the COP name (audit rename proposal).

Both convert the actor position with pixel >> 4 (no −1 row adjustment, unlike TileCollisionQuery / ParseSignedTileOffset in cop_handlers_collision) and read the byte through [$80],Y after CalcTileMapOffset (Y ≥ $4000 = out of the map). The handlers return by writing the next script address to the COP frame ($02,S) and RTI.
cop_handlers_actor_query:
COP handlers that query the player or linked actors (Bank 00, COP #44-#49 in hex = copdef ids 68-73).

#44 BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles and #45 BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles test whether the player actor is inside a tile rectangle and branch (four bytes: minX, minY, maxX, maxY, then a &Code target). #46/#47 copy this actor's position to its previous/next linked actor. #48 GetPlayerFacing returns the player's facing in A. #49 BranchIfBodyNe branches when characterForm differs from a byte.

Rectangle tests use unsigned compares with an exclusive lower bound and an inclusive upper bound (minX < player.X ≤ maxX, same for Y). Uses in extracted/: #44 44, #45 140, #48 6; #46, #47 and #49 have no users.
cop_handlers_audio:
COP handlers for SPC700 audio communication and music playback (Bank $00, 8 COP handlers).

StartMusic (#04) allocates a thinker with AllocateActorAfter and sets its entry to SpcTransferMusicData for the asynchronous SPC upload. FadeThenStartMusic (#05) does the same but enters at SpcFadeOutHandshake, which first sends $F1 on APUIO0: the SPC engine's CmdFadeOut command (fade counters $30/$31 = $FF; docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md), so the 'fade' in the name is real but happens inside the SPC engine, not in 65816 code (answers OQ-61; whether it is audible before the following $01/$F0 commands is OQ-I021-2). Both OR $1000 into the thinker's $12 (it keeps running while the world is frozen, as in MusicJingleActor), clear $1000 in its $10 and store the track in chatPtr.

PlaySoundCh2 (#06), PlaySoundCh1 (#07) and PlaySoundBoth (#08) write the sfx queue bytes sfxQueueCh1/Ch2 ($06F8/$06F9); WriteApuIo1 (#09) and WriteApuIo0 (#0A) write APUIO1/APUIO0 ($2141/$2140) directly.

MusicAndText (#19) allocates a pooled actor with ActorPoolAllocator, appends it to the list tail, CopyActorState, sets it to MusicJingleActor and stores the three operands ($0026 track, $0020 text pointer, $0022 text bank). On pool exhaustion the track is dropped and only the text is shown inline through DialogStringRenderer, then displayModeFlags bit 7 is cleared.

Uses in extracted/: PlaySoundCh1 244, PlaySoundCh2 92, PlaySoundBoth 72, StartMusic 57, MusicAndText 22, FadeThenStartMusic 14, WriteApuIo0 7, WriteApuIo1 4.
cop_handlers_bg_rearrange:
Event-block background-change COP handlers (37655–37728, Bank 00).

- StageBgChange (COP #32): loads the event block named by a script byte into the event-block work variables; nothing is drawn yet.
- ApplyBgChange (COP #33): animates the staged tile swap to completion, one VRAM-queue batch per frame.
- StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx (COP #34): like StageBgChange but takes the index from the actor's deathActionIdx field (the event-block byte of the scene actor record) and queues SFX $0F first.

Scripts use them as a StageBgChange + ApplyBgChange pair (102 StageBgChange sites: switches, doors, breakable walls, statues, boss rooms, the ending) or via SpawnFieldRevealEffect (COP #34). Handlers return by writing the next script address into the COP stack frame ($02,S) and RTI.
cop_handlers_callbacks:
Per-actor event callback registration COP handlers (39527–39657, Bank 00).

Each handler reads its operand from the script stream ($0A), stores it in an actor-slot-indexed table in bank $7F (X = slot, from TYX), and returns by writing the advanced script address to the COP frame ($02,S) and RTI.

Callback slots (addresses are bases; the actor slot id is added): onHitCallback +0 (#58), onDodgeCallback +2 (#59), onDeathCallback +4 (#57, plus a bank byte at +6, so death hooks can live in another bank), onCollideCallback +8 (#5A), custom callback +$16 (#5E, labelled scratch1010+6). Consumers: hit_stagger_controller and combat_collision dispatch the hit, dodge, death and collide hooks; actor_pool clears them when a slot is initialised. The custom slot is read by combat_collision as an interaction handler for push hits (it overwrites the victim's entry point); other actors reuse the word for their own purposes (the mummy queen stores a different value there, read back by pyDD_queen_spirit_attack).

OrExtraFlags (#5B) and AndExtraFlags (#5C) edit the actor's extendedFlags word ($7F002A). AndExtraFlags keeps only the bits in its mask (it does not clear them). Bits identified from their readers: $0002 moving, $0004 run after the actor list, $0008 ClearSolidHere on defeat, $0020 skip hit-stun, $0080 boss.
cop_handlers_collision:
Collision-layer COP handlers and their shared helpers (Bank 00). The block is not contiguous: the handlers sit at 34934–35864, SetCollisionAbs at 38191–38250, and the helpers at 44943–46208.

The collision layer ($7FC000, collisionLayer) holds one byte per 16×16-pixel tile: the high nibble ($F0) marks the tile solid/occupied (actors paint it with the MarkSolid* ops), the low nibble is the terrain type. Map indices use the page layout described in tile_collision_physics (16×16-tile pages, $10 bytes per tile row, mapRowStrideL0 pages per page row). Tile scratch lives in WRAM $0018 (X) and $001C (Y), reached through absolute addressing because D is zeroed inside the helpers.

Paint ops (script call sites): MarkSolidHere #0B (462), ClearSolidHere #0C (163), MarkSolidOffset #0D (20), ClearSolidOffset #0E (11), MarkSolidAbs #0F (86), ClearSolidAbs #10 (60), ClearCollisionHere #11 (9), ClearTypeAbs #12 (27), SetCollisionAbs #42 (1). "Here" ops cover the actor's metasprite hitbox rectangle; Offset and Abs ops touch a single tile.

Probe ops: BranchIfSolidHere/Offset/North/South/West/East #13–#18 (27/160/75/78/67/71), the type probes #1A–#1E (9/4/6/4/4), BranchIfNotOnGridline #1F. The type probes appear as BranchIfSolidType* in copdef.json; the handler labels here (BranchIfSolidType ... BranchIfSolidTypeEast) use different names. All probes go through TileCollisionQuery, which returns $000F for a blocked (high nibble set) or out-of-bounds probe and the tile's own low-nibble type otherwise, so a type operand of $0F cannot tell a solid tile from a non-solid tile of type $0F. Handlers return by writing the next script address to the COP frame ($02,S) and RTI.

Helpers: ParseSignedTileOffset (used by MarkSolidOffset, ClearSolidOffset), ComputeDirectionToPlayer (used by cop_handlers_player_query), MarkCollisionRect / ClearCollisionRect / ClearCollisionRectFull / AdvanceMapY (rectangle paint), and TileCollisionQuery (used by every probe here and by the WallAnim handlers in cop_handlers_player_sprite). The Offset and Abs handlers do not range-check the index returned by TileCoordsToMapIndex (the rectangle helpers do).
cop_handlers_dialog:
COP handlers for BG3 console scripts and dialogue text (Bank $00).

RunBg3Script (COP #BD), DialogueOptions (COP #BE), PrintDialogString (COP #BF) and PrintDialogStringAlt (COP #6B). Each reads its operands through [$0A] and returns to the actor script by writing the advanced $0A into the return frame ($02,S) and executing RTI.

The three dialogue handlers save and clear two pieces of state while the renderer runs and restore them afterwards: actor $10 bit 11 ($0800, cutscene-active; cleared so that RunActors_CutsceneOnly, run by the renderer's frame updates, does not re-run this actor — inferred) and joypadMaskStd (the buttons suppressed from joypadCurrent; cleared so the renderer sees every button).
cop_handlers_dungeon_switch:
Dungeon kill-tracking and switch-case COP handlers (44162–44225, Bank 00).

- SetDungeonKillFlag (COP #D8): records the current enemy's defeat in the wramFlags bitfield ($0A80). That field is cleared only on world map entry, by two scripts and on game over, so a kill can outlive the room (OQ-67).
- SwitchCase (COP #D9): computed jump through a word table in the script bank.

Both handlers return to the script by storing the next script address in the saved COP stack frame ($02,S) and executing RTI.
cop_handlers_effects:
COP handlers for sine-wave HDMA effects, gravity, spiral orbits and camera panning (Bank $00, 11 COP handlers + 2 internal subroutines).

Sine HDMA. InitSineHdma (COP #5F) takes a WRAM base and a wave period n (scanlines per HDMA entry; #08–#40 observed) and builds four indirect-HDMA tables at base, +$0200, +$0400 and +$0600. Each table holds 256/n three-byte entries (line count n | $80 = repeat mode, data pointer) that all point at the same n data words at table + $0100, so one sine period repeats down the 256 scanlines. Tables 1 and 2 are the even/odd frame buffers for the horizontal scroll and tables 3 and 4 those for the vertical scroll; one BindSineHdma per axis binds the pair. TickSineHdma (COP #60) advances a delay counter and the sine phase and rebuilds the data of the current frame's buffers from a camera coordinate (BuildSineHdmaTable). BindSineHdma (COP #61) binds a table (+$0200 on odd frames) to an HDMA channel through SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect. The effect actor keeps its table base in spritesetPtr, the amplitude in $7F0008 (the spriteset bank field, unused by these non-sprite actors), the phase in retPtr1 and the delay counter in animScratch+2.

Gravity. InitGravity (COP #63) seeds the initial upward speed v0, a shift factor f and a target Y (moveYAlt = Y + tile offset × 16). TickGravity (COP #64) increments a tick counter t and sets the Y delta moveScratch2 = ((t × (t >> 1)) >> f) − v0 (ApplyMovement consumes it), returning A = $FFFF once the actor has moved down past the target Y and A = $0000 otherwise.

Spiral. InitSpiral (COP #6C) stores orbitDiameter and orbitAngle (256 angle units = one turn). SpiralStep (COP #6D) adds signed deltas to both and calls ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef with the reference actor in $0000 (the script stores it there first), so the actor circles or spirals around that actor. Only mu67_vampires uses them.

Camera pan. CameraPanDown/Up/Right/Left (COP #DC–#DF) move cameraTargetY/X by the step in the low nibble of $2B every call. $2A counts the calls left on the current step; when it underflows the next table word is fetched with CameraScrollStepLookup (low byte = delay → $2A, high byte = step → $2B; a zero high byte ends the table and the script resumes). They yield with PLA PLA RTL until the target reaches cameraBoundsY/X (down/right) or passes cameraOffsetY/X (up/left).

Internal: BuildSineHdmaTable generates per-scanline scroll offsets from sine_table_8bit via hardware multiply into the double-buffered WRAM tables. BuildSineLookupTable fills the two 256-word arrays sineTableA/B with amplitude-scaled sine values, guarded by displayModeFlags/animScratch2 trigger bits.
cop_handlers_flags:
Exported JSL flag helper library and core flag routines for the eventFlags ($0A00) and wramFlags ($0A80) bitfields (Bank $00, 5 core routines + 14 JSL helpers + 1 data table).

Core routines: SetEventFlag/ClearEventFlag/TestEventFlag decompose a flag index into byte (÷8) and bit (AND $07) indices using the bitmasks_bit_position lookup table, then OR/AND/test the corresponding bit in the eventFlags array at $0A00. SetWramFlag/TestWramFlag perform the same operation on the wramFlags array at $0A80.

JSL offset wrappers add base offsets ($0100, $0200, $0300, $0510) before calling the core routines, providing scoped flag access for different game systems: $0100 for boss/dungeon defeat flags, $0200 for persistent world events (chests, Red Jewels), $0300 for scene-scoped state, $0510 for late-game progression. TestFlagRaw/SetFlagRaw/ClearFlagRaw access flags without offset.

ClearAllWramFlags zero-fills the entire $20-byte wramFlags region. bitmasks_bit_position is a shared 8-byte table mapping indices 0–7 to mask bytes $01–$80.

The COP handlers that call these routines (SetFlagByte/Word, ClearFlagByte/Word, BranchOnFlagByte/Word, WaitOnFlagByte/Word, GiveItem, RemoveItem, BranchIfHasItem, BranchIfItemEquipped, SetDungeonKillFlag) are in cop_handlers_flow.
cop_handlers_flow:
COP handlers for script control flow, event flags, inventory management, and timer waits (Bank $00, 30 COP handlers).

Script control flow (14 handlers): SetInteractHandler stores NPC interaction pointers in chatPtr. SetEntryHere/HereAndYield/Far set or save entry points for yielding actors. JumpAfterDelay/NextFrame/Far implement deferred and cross-bank jumps. CallNear/Deferred provide subroutine calls with return PC saved in retPtr1. RestoreSavedPtr/ReturnWithSignal restore deferred call pointers. SetSavedPtr stores return addresses for later restoration. LoopStart/LoopEnd implement counted iteration with separate player (loopCounter/$7F0014) and scene actor (loopCounterActor/$7F2102) loop state.

Event flag handlers (8): SetFlagByte/Word and ClearFlagByte/Word set or clear bits in the eventFlags bitfield via cop_handlers_flags core routines. BranchOnFlagByte/Word branch based on flag state with a sense operand (0=branch-on-clear, nonzero=branch-on-set). WaitOnFlagByte/Word yield each frame until a flag condition is met by rewinding the entry PC.

Inventory and state (5): GiveItem calls GiveItemToPlayer with carry-based overflow branching. RemoveItem removes by item ID. BranchIfHasItem/BranchIfItemEquipped test inventory state. SetDungeonKillFlag records enemy kills in wramFlags.

Misc (3): SwitchCase dispatches through a word-aligned jump table indexed by a WRAM byte. WaitByte/WaitWord set frame delay timers and yield.
cop_handlers_force_move:
Force-move COP handlers ($AA–$B1, 8 opcodes): stage movement delta chains and flip movement direction.

A movement index (0-$54) selects a delta chain in move_chain_table: a linked list of nodes, each a signed per-frame delta plus a link to the next node. StageMoveX/Y/XY store the index in moveXAlt/moveYAlt ($7F:0018/$7F:001A + actor slot) and put the chain pointer that AnimFrameLookup returns in actor field $2C (X chain) or $2E (Y chain); ApplyMovement and the collision-checked move in tile_collision_physics consume one node per frame from each chain.

SetMoveNegateX/NE/Both set (operand nonzero) or clear (operand 0) $12 bit $4000 (negate the X delta), bit $2000 (negate the Y delta), or both ($6000). ApplyMoveToChild stages both indices on the newest actor in the list ($0058, actorListLast) instead of the caller. ReloadMoveChains re-runs the lookup for the current indices, which rewinds $2C/$2E to the start of their chains.

Each handler reads its operand bytes through the script pointer [$0A], advances $0A, and writes it back into the stacked return address ($02,S) before RTI. Entry has Y = actor slot (TYX).
cop_handlers_hdma_dma:
HDMA channel COP handlers (34382–34579, Bank 00): GenHdmaSine (#00), QueueHdma (#01), QueueHdmaDirect (#02) and QueueHdmaChannel (#03), 51 script sites in total.

Shared operand layout for #01–#03: a 3-byte table address followed by a byte naming the PPU B-bus register ($21xx, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS, #26 = WH0, #1B = M7A). The setup helpers (hdma_dma_spc) use that register number as the index into hdma_channel_config to get the DMAP transfer mode, so the table is really "PPU register → transfer mode".

All three bind an HDMA channel: #01 uses indirect addressing, #02 uses direct addressing (despite the name it is not a plain DMA), and #03 programs a caller-chosen channel instead of the next free one. Channel allocation starts at channel 1 and is reset by ResetHdmaState. #00 prepares the sine-wave table that #01 then binds.
cop_handlers_input:
COP handlers for joypad polling (Bank $00, 4 handlers, COP #3E–#41; the Branch pair has about 190 call sites in the vanilla scripts, the Wait pair none).

Every handler takes a 16-bit button mask operand (joypad bit layout: B $8000, Y $4000, Select $2000, Start $1000, Up $0800, Down $0400, Left $0200, Right $0100, A $0080, X $0040, L $0020, R $0010). Bit 0 of the mask is never a button, so it is used as the source selector:
- bit 0 clear: test joypadCurrent, the held buttons minus any consumed or masked ones (joypadHeld, joypadMaskStd; see vblank_joypad)
- bit 0 set: test joypadRaw, the remapped held state with no consumption or masking applied

WaitForButton/WaitForRelease (unused by the vanilla scripts) yield via RTL (re-running themselves next frame) until the test passes. BranchIfPressed/BranchIfNotPressed branch immediately on the same test. The world-map staging handlers are in cop_handlers_world_map; RunBg3Script and the dialogue handlers are in cop_handlers_dialog.
cop_handlers_inventory:
Inventory COP handlers (44037–44161, Bank 00).

Script-level wrappers around inventory_mgmt:
- GiveItem (COP #D4): add an item, branch to an overflow target when the inventory is full (49 sites).
- RemoveItem (COP #D5): remove an item by ID (34 sites).
- BranchIfHasItem (COP #D6): branch when the item is in the inventory (35 sites).
- BranchIfItemEquipped (COP #D7): branch when the operand matches the equipped item (5 sites).

The branch operands are &Code offsets in the script bank. Handlers return by writing the resume address into the COP stack frame ($02,S) and RTI.
cop_handlers_lifecycle:
COP handlers for actor death, removal, callbacks, position queries, movement staging, OAM attributes, and extended flags (Bank $00, 37 COP handlers + 2 internal routines).

Callback setters: SetDeathCallback, SetHitCallback, SetDodgeCallback, SetCollideCallback, SetCustomCallback write script pointers into WRAM callback fields ($7F1000–$7F1016). OrExtraFlags/AndExtraFlags modify the extendedFlags word ($7F002A).

SetLinkedEntryPtr writes a far script pointer into the linked actor's entry fields. BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles/AbsTiles test whether the player falls inside a tile rectangle. CopyPosToPrev/Next copy position to adjacent list actors. GetPlayerFacing loads player direction. BranchIfBodyNe branches on characterForm.

MarkDeath/Die handle actor death — Die with child flag $0040 routes through DieExit to cascade-remove children by parentId, then patches the doubly-linked list. MarkDeathResumeHandler restores actor context after MarkDeath's PEA/RTS dispatch. KillPrev/KillNext remove adjacent actors.

StageMoveX/Y/XY set movement deltas via AnimFrameLookup. SetMoveNegateX/NE/Both set direction bits on $0012. ApplyMoveToChild propagates move to the child actor. ReloadMoveChains refreshes frame durations without changing indices. SetPriorityMax/Min/ClearPriorityMax/Min control draw priority bits. SetSpritePriority/Palette write OAM attribute fields. Mirror toggles (ToggleHMirror/VMirror, ClearHMirror, SetHMirror) flip sprites. NudgePosition applies signed pixel offsets.
cop_handlers_linked_actor:
COP handler for SetLinkedEntryPtr ($6A), the only linked-actor operation (40454–40482, Bank 00).

Retargets the actor that follows the caller in the actor list (nextActorLink, $06): writes a new 16-bit script pointer into that actor's entryPtr and clears its waitCounter ($08) and velocity ($2C/$2E). The caller's own entry pointer is not touched, and the caller keeps running after the operand.

Usage: all 164 call sites are in ending/ending_credits (sF7_credits*.asm), where a director actor alternates HaltIfMaxFrames with SetLinkedEntryPtr to step a linked child (Will's sprite, marchers) through animation scripts on a frame timeline. The caller must already have a valid $06 link.
cop_handlers_map:
COP handlers for metatile painting, world-map streaming, VRAM DMA, decompression, and occlusion queries (Bank $00, 12 COP handlers + 3 internal subroutines).

DrawMetatileAbs/Here write a metatile ID to mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer, queue BG VRAM tile writes when on-screen. DrawMetatileStream/4 parse sequential map-entry records (3 or 4 bytes) to stream tile changes with optional SFX.

AdhocVramDma stages a one-off VRAM DMA transfer gated by extendedFlags bit 0. CopyPalette transfers palette data between CGRAM staging areas. Decompress calls QuintetLzDecompress and clears the actor render list. SetScratchPointer writes a far pointer into animScratch fields.

BranchIfBehindWall tests tile-layer occlusion via CalcTileMapOffset. BranchIfCollisionTypeEq branches when the tile type nibble differs from an operand. BranchIfOffCamera compares actor position against camera bounds. HaltIfMaxFrames yields when the frame counter exceeds a threshold.

Internal: ParseMapEntry decodes tile X/Y/ID from a 3-byte stream record; returns carry set on end sentinel. ResolveTileData converts tile coordinates to a map-layer index, writes metatile and collision bytes, and queues VRAM tile updates when the tile is on-screen. TileQueryGate prevents concurrent tile queries by yielding RTL when tileQueryResult is non-zero.
cop_handlers_metatile:
COP handlers that overwrite one metatile of LAYER 0 at run time (Bank 00, COP #4B-#4E) plus their helpers. Used by puzzle rooms, breakable walls and the item-use effects to swap floor/wall tiles.

Script sites: DrawMetatileAbs (#4B) 24, DrawMetatileHere (#4C) 8 (2 in pyD0_breakable_wall, 6 in item_use_system). DrawMetatileStream (#4D) and DrawMetatileStreamDelay (#4E) have no script sites.

All writes go to layer 0 only: collision flags come from $7F0000 + metatile ID (the layer-0 table; collisionFlagTableL1 sits at $7F0100 and is not used here), the map is $7EA000 + index (mapLayerTilemap), the collision map is $7FC000 + index, and the tile definitions are read from the hard-coded $7E2000 + ID x 8 (metatileDefBase is $2000 for layer 0, $2800 for layer 1). A tile is repainted on screen only when it lies in the visible window: horizontally (pixel X + 16 - bg1ScrollH) < $0111, vertically 0 <= pixel Y - ((mapScrollV - $10) and $FFF0) < $F1. Off-screen tiles only update the map and collision data.
The staged update is one 2x2 metatile: $0902 = VRAM word address of the top row (BG1 nametable at $1000 via PixelToVramAddress), $0908 = that + $20, tile words $0904/$0906 (top) and $090A/$090C (bottom). The NMI flush in event_blocks writes it and clears $0902; TileQueryGate makes the next draw wait until $0902 is zero again. The name tileQueryResult is a misnomer.

Direct page: the handlers run with D = actor; the stores to $0018/$001A/$001C/$001E/$0000 are absolute (page-0 scratch) and become the DP $18/$1A/$1C/$1E/$00 seen by ResolveTileData after TCD zeroes D. The page-0 $00 here is NOT the actor's entry word. DrawMetatileHere takes the actor's $14/$16 as TILE coordinates (no divide by 16); pyD0_breakable_wall converts its pixel position first and saves the originals in orbitAngle/orbitDiameter ($7F0010/$7F0012).
DrawMetatileStream/4 stream one 3- or 4-byte record per call (X tile, Y tile, metatile ID, and for #4E a delay byte stored in the actor's $08 wait counter), cache the pointer in $24, rewind the script pointer by 2 and yield between tiles, and an X byte with bit 7 set ends the stream. extendedFlags ($7F002A) bit 1 = pointer cached, bit 2 = queue orbitAngle as a sound effect (sfxQueueCh2) per tile; nothing in the extracted scripts uses them.
cop_handlers_movement:
COP handlers for smooth interpolated movement, grid snapping, proximity testing and RNG (Bank $00, 9 COP handlers + 10 internal subroutines).

BranchIfActorNear/BranchIfPlayerNear test a square box: both |ΔX| and |ΔY| must be ≤ radius × 16 px (the code compares against radius × 16 + 1). BranchIfActorNear has no call site in extracted/. ResolveActorIndex converts an 8-bit actor list index to a WRAM pointer ($1000 + index × $30).

MoveToward is a yielding handler that moves the actor to the target in moveXAlt/moveYAlt (set up by the calling script) at a speed given in px/frame: frames = larger-axis distance ÷ speed (UnsignedDivide), stored +1 as the tick limit. Each tick it computes the offset travelled so far per axis (tick × distance ÷ frames), subtracts what was already applied, and hands the signed difference to ApplyMovement through moveScratch1/2. Distances are capped at $FE per axis, and when the distance is smaller than the speed the quotient is 0 and the actor does not move (OQ-56). InitSmoothMovement does the first-entry setup and sets extendedFlags bit 1; MoveTowardFinish clears it.

The hardware math pipeline uses chained helpers: MultiplyThenDivide feeds WRMPYB → RDMPYL → WRDIVL → RDDIVL for the cumulative offset, with ReadMultiplyResult (1 NOP) and ReadDivideResult (5 NOPs) providing the hardware latency delays. MovementVelocityCompute wraps the same pipeline for TickMove's per-axis calculations.

SnapToGrid yields to EnemyPositionSnap until the actor aligns to the 16×16 tile grid. ResumeAfterSnap restores the script pointer from snapResumePtr.

StageMove/TickMove split the same interpolation into a setup COP and a per-frame COP. StageMove reads animation, speed and a duration-cap operand, stores |dx|, |dy|, the two sign bits (animScratch2 bits 14/15) and the frame count, and halves both distances via HalveMovementDistance until the larger fits in a byte; each halving adds one extra pass, handled by TickMoveComplete. A speed operand ≥ $80 is negated to |speed| and also triggers one more halving pass (the BCC after the divide tests the carry left by CMP #$80), roughly halving the speed (OQ-55).

RngByte steps a 16-byte additive generator ($0410–$041F: each byte += the next byte + carry, then a ripple counter is incremented); it is not an LFSR. RngMod reduces the last RngByte output by repeated subtraction (a modulus of 0 would hang).

CameraScrollStepLookup reads scroll speed entries from scrollStepTableBase for the four CameraPan COP handlers in cop_handlers_effects.
cop_handlers_oam_attribs:
COP handlers for actor depth priority, OAM attribute mask and position nudging (42931–43111, Bank 00).

Ten COP opcodes ($B2–$BB) plus NudgePosition ($BC), all with the standard handler shape: TYX, change one field of the calling actor, then store the operand pointer $0A to the return address on the stack ($02,S) and RTI.

=== DEPTH PRIORITY ($B2–$B5) ===

Set or clear bits of the actor flag word $10 that override the Y-based sort key of SortActorsByDepth. Bit 1 ($0002, SetPriorityMax) forces key $0000: first OAM index, drawn in front of every other actor. Bit 0 ($0001, SetPriorityMin) forces key $01FE: last OAM index, drawn behind every other actor. Max wins when both are set. Typical use: a falling or flying actor takes Max while airborne (ceiling tiles, seagulls, falling orbs) and drops to Min once it rests on the floor. The only reader of these two bits found in the extracted code is the depth sort; older docs call them 'collision priority', which the code does not support.

=== OAM ATTRIBUTE MASK ($B6–$BB) ===

Actor word $0E is an XOR mask that DecomposeActorMetasprites applies to every sub-sprite's tile/attribute word (UpdateActorAnimation also reads its flip bits): $3000 = OAM priority (BG layer order), $0E00 = palette, $4000 = H-flip, $8000 = V-flip. SetSpritePriority and SetSpritePalette clear their field, then merge the operand (0–3 / 0–7) shifted into the high byte. The mirror handlers EOR (Toggle), TRB (Clear) or TSB (Set) the flip bit. Script-side names in copdef.json are SetSpritePriority and SetSpritePalette.

=== NUDGE ($BC) ===

NudgePosition adds two signed byte operands to the actor's pixel position ($14/$16). It is a position operation that happens to sit with the attribute handlers.
cop_handlers_offscreen:

- BranchIfOffCamera (COP #68): branch when the actor lies outside the camera's scroll window.
- HaltIfMaxFrames (COP #69): hold the script until the global timeline counter $00E4 exceeds a threshold.

BranchIfOffCamera returns by storing the next script address in the saved COP frame ($02,S) and executing RTI. HaltIfMaxFrames either does the same or, while waiting, rewinds the actor's entry pointer and yields with RTL.
cop_handlers_palette:
Palette-bundle animation COP handlers (37729–37887, Bank 00): five ops, #36–#3A (177 script sites). The block holds only these five handlers; the BG event-block ops live in cop_handlers_bg_rearrange and the thinker spawn/kill ops in cop_handlers_thinker.

A palette bundle (palette_bundles table, selected by a byte ID) is a list of 6-byte sub-entries; each sub-entry is an animation STRIP of N frames (byte 0), every frame being a block of consecutive colors copied to the same palette destination, and the frames of a strip are stored back to back. LoadPaletteBundle (hdma_dma_spc) loads the next sub-entry and CopyPaletteBundleFrame copies one frame (an MVN block move) per step. Per-actor state: bundle ID in animScratch+2 ($7F0002), sub-entry index in DP $0E (reset to 0 when the bundle ends), frames left in the strip in spritesetPtr ($7F0006, loaded from byte 0 of the sub-entry), the source pointer of the next frame in chatPtr, the wait value (sub-entry byte 5) in animScratch ($7F0000) and DP $08, and the pass counter in retPtr1 ($7F0004) for the Loop variants.

Start ops (#36–#38) load and apply sub-entry 0, store the address after the op in the actor entry point ($00) and YIELD (PLA, PLA, RTL), so on the next frame the script resumes right after the Start op. Step ops (#39, #3A) must therefore directly follow the Start op (the ambient thinkers do exactly this): each frame a Step either keeps yielding or, when the bundle (and, for #3A, every pass) is finished, continues the script with RTI.

Typical use: ambient_palette_cycler (PaletteRestart + PaletteStep in a loop; the bundle ID is the thinker's spawn parameter), one-shot palette flash thinkers, boot logos, boss and ability palette effects. PaletteStartLoop/StepLoop have three sites (two attack_ability_system ability effects and one unused script).
cop_handlers_player_query:
COP handlers that place an actor, stage map changes and compare the actor's position with the player's (Bank $00; COP #25–#31 and #35).

SetTilePos puts the actor on a tile. QueueMapChange stages a scene change (sceneNext, spawn X/Y, facing/flags, scroll parameters at $0642–$0652) and can record a revive/save warp point. WaitWhileOffscreen polls the actor's off-screen flag. The query handlers compare the actor's pixel position ($14/$16) with the player's; all deltas are signed 16-bit (player − actor).

- BranchIfPlayerAt / BranchIfActorAt: exact pixel match.
- BranchOnPlayerX / BranchOnPlayerY: three-way branch (zero delta or |Δ| below the threshold → centre; otherwise west/east or above/below).
- BranchNearerAxis: branch on whether |ΔX| or |ΔY| is larger.
- DirToPlayer / DirToPlayerFrom return the 0–7 direction from ComputeDirectionToPlayer in A; BranchIfDirToPlayer / ...From branch when it equals an operand.
- CardinalToPlayer returns 0–3 = N/E/S/W for the dominant axis (ties go to the vertical axis).
- BranchOnPlayerFacing branches on GetPlayerFacingDirection, whose order is 0 = down, 1 = up, 2 = left, 3 = right (not the N/E/S/W order of CardinalToPlayer).

Every handler exits with RTI after storing the new script PC at $02,S.
cop_handlers_player_sprite:
COP handlers for the player's body spriteset and player-specific animation staging (Bank 00, 11 handlers, COP #8E-#98). The copdef names for #90-#92 are StagePlayerMoveX/Y/XY (the labels here are StagePlayerMoveX/Y/XY).

Script sites: SetPlayerSpriteDirect 24, StagePlayerSprite 93, StagePlayerMoveX 2, MoveY 21, MoveXY 9, RunPlayerAnim 8, StagePlayerSprFromDP 8 (all in forced_walk). StagePlayerSprWall and WallAnimHere/North/South have no script sites.

=== Body table ===
SetPlayerSpriteDirect takes an index into the 6-byte body_table entries (word spriteset pointer, bank byte, ...): 0 Will ($95), 1 Freedan ($8E), 2 and 3 Shadow ($94), 4 will_alt ($8F), 5 ability_fx ($8F), 6 freedan_fx ($97), 7 shadow_fx ($97), 8 shadow_mode ($97). It writes spritesetPtr ($7F0006), the bank byte ($7F0008), the table offset into animScratch2 ($7F000E, read by the sprite decomposer while playerFlags bit 15 is set) and the raw index into $0AC8, then sets playerFlags $8000. It does NOT stage an animation: no $28/$2A change. $7F0008 is polymorphic (sprite bank for sprite actors, amplitude for HDMA sine thinkers).
The StagePlayerSprite family calls SetActorBody instead, which picks the body from characterForm, so one script works for Will, Freedan and Shadow.

=== Staging ===
These ops store the raw animation operand in $28 (no ProcessAnimFlag, so no mirror handling), clear $2A, and save the next-op address in $00 and the script bank in $02 (the lines LDA $0C / STA $02 before each store are inserted by db-us/transforms.json and have no address tag). The movement operands of MoveX/MoveY/MoveXY are movement indices, not distances or durations: AnimFrameLookup turns each into the head of a delta chain (move_chain_table) stored in $2C (X) or $2E (Y); moveXAlt/moveYAlt ($7F0018/$7F001A) keep the raw index. StagePlayerSprFromDP takes the animation index from the actor's $00 word, which the forced_walk helpers ReadDirSprite_* park there just before; the handler then overwrites $00 with the new entry address. RunPlayerAnim behaves exactly like AnimOnce (#89).

=== WallAnimHere/North/South (#96-#98, unused) ===
Take a joypad mask word and compare it with joypadCurrent for equality; on mismatch they continue without waiting. Only the Y alignment is checked (Y low nibble must be 0); when misaligned they animate without probing. The probe tile is at the actor (Here), Y - $10 (North) or Y + $10 (South). TileCollisionQuery already folds solid tiles and out-of-bounds into $000F, so the BIT #$00F0 test never fires and only the $000F compare detects a block (the actor flag $0004 is then set and the op continues). Otherwise, when the tile type equals playerWallType ($09B0) they run UpdateActorAnimation (yield while it runs, continue when it finishes); a different type continues without animating. $0018/$001C are the page-0 scratch pair read by TileCollisionQuery.
cop_handlers_scene_flags:
COP handlers for the persistent event-flag bitfield — set, clear, branch and wait (43841–44037, Bank 00).

Eight COP opcodes ($CC–$D3, copdef ids 204–211) operate on the 2048-bit eventFlags field at $0A00 through flag_helpers (SetEventFlag, ClearEventFlag, TestEventFlag). Every opcode comes in a Byte form (flag index 0–$FF, one operand byte) and a Word form (index 0–$7FF, two operand bytes). Script usage in the extracted code (COP [..] sites): SetFlagByte 475, SetFlagWord 62, ClearFlagByte 71, ClearFlagWord 22, BranchOnFlagByte 630, BranchOnFlagWord 40, WaitOnFlagByte 384, WaitOnFlagWord 9.

=== SENSE BYTE ===

Branch and Wait take a sense byte after the flag index: 0 means 'act when the flag is clear', nonzero means 'act when the flag is set'. BranchOnFlag then reads a &Code word (the branch target within the script bank); WaitOnFlag has no target.

=== SHARED TAILS ===

The Byte forms of Branch and Wait read their flag index, call TestEventFlag and then jump into the sense-byte tail that sits inside the Word form (BranchOnFlagByte uses loc_00AB9A / loc_00ABA5, WaitOnFlagByte uses loc_00ABE9 / loc_00ABF4). Those labels belong to the Word handlers' bodies, and the Byte forms reach them with relative branches, so the forms must stay within branch range of each other.

=== RETURN CONVENTIONS ===

Set, Clear and Branch finish by storing the advanced operand pointer ($0A) over the return address ($02,S) and RTI. WaitOnFlag first stores the address of its own COP opcode (operand pointer − 2) in the actor's re-entry word ($00); while the flag does not match it yields with PLA PLA RTL, so the same COP re-runs next frame.
cop_handlers_script_control:
COP script-control handlers (Bank $00): interaction handler, resume entry, jumps, calls and loops (COP #C0–#CB, #E1, #E2).

An actor script resumes from the entry pointer in its DP: $00/$01 = offset, $02 = bank. SetEntryHere and SetEntryHereAndYield save the position after themselves; JumpAfterDelay, JumpNextFrame, SetEntryFar and JumpFar write a target. Yielding handlers pop the COP frame and RTL (the actor resumes next frame at $00/$02); the others RTI back into the stream. SetEntryFar only changes the entry and keeps running; JumpFar also jumps.

Call/return uses a single slot, retPtr1 ($7F0004), so calls do not nest. SetSavedPtr stores an explicit &Code operand; CallNear and CallNearDeferred store the address after their own operand and jump to the target. RestoreSavedPtr and ReturnWithSignal jump back to the slot and clear it, or yield when it is empty (ReturnWithSignal also returns A = $FFFF).

Loops: LoopStart saves the count and the loop-head PC, LoopEnd decrements the count and, until it reaches zero, sets $00 to the loop head and yields (so at least one frame per iteration). A count of 0 would wrap to 65536 iterations (no guard). Pooled actors (X ≥ $1000) keep the count and head in their own fields loopCounter ($7F0014) and retPtr2 ($7F001E). Thinkers (X < $1000) use the arrays loopCounterActor ($7F2102) and loopStartPcActor ($7F2100) indexed by X; those two mnemonic names say 'Actor' but they are the thinker variants (rename proposal 90).

SetInteractHandler (#C0, 322 uses in scripts) stores a &Code pointer in chatPtr ($7F000A), the routine the interaction system runs when the player talks to or touches the actor.

COP handlers for collision layer manipulation, DMA/HDMA queue operations, and tile collision queries (Bank $00, 25 COP handlers + 7 internal routines).

DMA/HDMA queue: GenHdmaSine builds a 512-entry sine wave via the hardware multiplier and writes a 3-entry HDMA indirect table. QueueHdma/QueueHdmaDirect/QueueHdmaChannel set up HDMA and DMA channel registers.

Solid marking: MarkSolidHere/Offset/Abs OR $F0 onto collisionLayer tiles. ClearSolidHere/Offset/Abs AND $0F to remove solid flags. ClearCollisionHere clears both nibbles. ClearTypeAbs clears only the type nibble.

Solid branching: BranchIfSolidHere/Offset/North/South/West/East test the solid nibble at directional offsets. BranchIfSolidType/North/South/West/East compare the type nibble against an operand. BranchIfNotOnGridline checks 16px alignment.

SetCollisionAbs writes a full collision byte at absolute tile coordinates.

Internal: MarkCollisionRect/ClearCollisionRect/ClearCollisionRectFull iterate over metasprite hitbox tiles. ParseSignedTileOffset decodes signed tile offsets. ComputeDirectionToPlayer computes 8-direction index. TileCollisionQuery samples a tile via CalcTileMapOffset. AdvanceMapY handles row wrapping.
cop_handlers_spatial:
COP handlers for direction computation, position branching, and map transitions (Bank $00, 14 COP handlers + 1 internal stub).

SetTilePos converts byte tile coordinates to pixel positions ($14/$16). QueueMapChange writes scene/position/flag data for map transitions with optional save-restore.

WaitWhileOffscreen yields when actor flag $4000 (off-screen) is set. BranchIfPlayerAt/BranchIfActorAt compare exact pixel coordinates. BranchOnPlayerX/Y perform 3-way branches (left/center/right or above/center/below) based on distance thresholds. BranchNearerAxis branches on the closer axis.

DirToPlayer/CardinalToPlayer/DirToPlayerFrom compute direction indices (0–7 or 0–3) from the actor to the player. BranchIfDirToPlayer/From branch on computed direction. BranchOnPlayerFacing dispatches on the player's 4-way facing direction.

Internal: CardinalToPlayer_Exit is the return epilogue for CardinalToPlayer's RTS-trick dispatch.
cop_handlers_spawn:
COP handlers for actor spawning — the SpawnBefore/After/Abs/Offset/Marked family plus list append (Bank $00, 14 COP handlers, ids $99-$A6).

SpawnBefore*/SpawnAfter* call AllocateActorBefore/AllocateActorAfter, which link a new actor beside the spawner and CopyActorState (clones $0E, $10 with $2000 set, $12 without bit 12, position and more from the spawner). The handler then writes the entry address (word at $0000, bank at $0002) and any operands: position offsets are added to the inherited $14/$16, absolute positions replace them, a flags word replaces $0010.

The Marked variants (SpawnBeforeMarked, SpawnAfterMarked, SpawnAfterAbsMarked, SpawnAfterOffsetMarked) set $0040 in the spawner's own $12 (Die cascades to marked children) and call MarkChildActor, which sets the new actor's parentId to the spawner's parentId, or to the spawner itself when it has none.

SpawnListAppend/SpawnListAppendSpr use ActorPoolAllocator and append at the tail of the actor list ($0058); on pool exhaustion they skip all operand bytes without spawning. SpawnListAppendSpr also reads an animation index (stored at $0028).

Uses in extracted/: SpawnListAppend 256, SpawnAfterFlags 231, SpawnAfterOffsetFlags 126, SpawnAfterAbsFlags 106, SpawnAfterMarked 101, SpawnAfterOffsetMarked 77; SpawnAfterOffset, SpawnAfterAbs and SpawnListAppendSpr have no users.
cop_handlers_sprite:
COP handlers for sprite animation, frame staging and spriteset assignment (Bank $00, 16 COP handlers + 1 internal routine).

=== FRAME-LIST ANIMATION (#80–#8D, 6,687 script sites) ===
An actor owns a spriteset table (spritesetPtr $7F0006 + bank $7F0008, set by SetMetasprite): word pointers, one frame list per animation index ($28). A frame list is a sequence of 4-byte records addressed by the frame counter $2A: word 0 = hold time, word 2 = pointer to the frame's sprite data; a negative word 0 ends the list. sprite_composition.UpdateActorAnimation reads the record, stores the hold time in DP $08 (the wait counter the actor runner decrements with DEC $08 / BPL skip, so a hold of n shows the frame for n + 1 ticks), sets metaspritePtr and the extents/hitbox, and increments $2A; at the end of a list it resets $2A and returns carry SET without staging anything.
- StageSpriteFrame (#80) and its Move/Loop variants only CHOOSE the animation: ProcessAnimFlag stores the index in $28 and clears $2A. Optional operands set the repeat count (sprTimer $7F0016: StageSpriteLoop*) and the movement chains (StageSpriteMove*: movement indices 0-$54 kept in moveXAlt/moveYAlt $7F0018/$7F001A, and the delta-chain heads from move_chain_table in $2C/$2E, exactly as StageMoveX/Y/XY in cop_handlers_force_move; the operands are indices, not distances or durations).
- AnimOnce (#89), AnimLoop (#8A), AnimOneFrame (#8B) and WaitForAnimFrame (#8C) PLAY it: each call runs UpdateActorAnimation and either yields (PLA PLA RTL; the entry point is unchanged, so the same op runs again after the hold) or continues with RTI. When a list ends they zero $2C/$2E, so the staged movement stops with the animation.
- StageSprAndHitbox (#8D) stages the animation and calls UpdateActorAnimation at once (no yield) to set the first frame's sprite and hitbox, then clears $2A again: it poses an actor without playing it.

=== Entry address and bank ===
SetTileStreamAnim and every StageSprite* op store the address after the op in $00 and so act like SetEntryHere: the actor re-enters at the next op. The Anim* ops yield WITHOUT touching $00, so a Stage* op before them makes the same Anim* op run again every time the actor runs until the animation finishes. The two lines LDA $0C / STA $02 in front of each such store have no address tag because db-us/transforms.json (cop_handlers_sprite) inserts them: they also store the script bank in $02, so the entry bank follows the op (the original ROM saved only $00).

=== TILE-STREAMING ANIMATION (#55 SetTileStreamAnim, #56 AdvanceSpriteAnim, 4 script sites) ===
Used by four effect actors (awB4_snake_pit_fx, fr32_laborer_npc ×2, dc2F_adrift_fx): a script runs SetScratchPointer (art source: word in animScratch, bank in animScratch+2), SetMetasprite, SetTileStreamAnim (animation index, VRAM word address in $24), then AdvanceSpriteAnim in a loop. Each AdvanceSpriteAnim call waits while the previous DMA is pending ($B2 nonzero), stages one frame (32 bytes, or 128 when the byte at +$0D of the frame's sprite data is nonzero) taken from animScratch + 32 × (byte at +$12) to the VRAM word address in $24 (the NMI performs the DMA), loads the hold time into $08 and yields. At the end of a list the counter restarts and the script continues past the op.

=== Animation index byte (ProcessAnimFlag) ===
$FF keeps the current index. Bit 7 selects the mirrored variant: the low 7 bits go to $28 and the horizontal flip bit $4000 of the OAM attribute word $0E is set; without bit 7 the flip bit is cleared. Both flip updates are skipped when bit 1 ($0002) of the actor status $12 is set: that bit is a persistent mirror lock, not a facing flag (awB0_zombie sets it after a mirrored StageSprAndHitbox and sE8_dark_gaia right after SetHMirror; OQ-I022-1).

Uses in extracted/: AnimOnce 2075, StageSpriteFrame 1200, AnimLoop 1048, StageSpriteLoop 455, StageSpriteMoveY 331, StageSpriteMoveX 310, StageSpriteLoopMoveX 278, StageSpriteLoopMoveY 252, StageSprAndHitbox 229, SetMetasprite 186, AnimOneFrame 165, StageSpriteMoveXY 68, StageSpriteLoopMoveXY 61, WaitForAnimFrame 29, SetTileStreamAnim 4, AdvanceSpriteAnim 4.
cop_handlers_thinker:
Thinker spawn/kill COP handlers (37888–38020, Bank 00).

Thinkers are lightweight actors taken from a separate pool (16 slots of $10 bytes at $0F00–$0FFF, free list at $7E:3000 via the long pointer $52/$54) and kept in their own doubly-linked list ($5A head / $5C tail), distinct from the scene actor list ($56/$58).

- SpawnThinkerParam (COP #3B): allocate a thinker, store a byte parameter in its animScratch+2 and set its entry point (21 sites).
- SpawnThinker (COP #3C): same without the parameter byte (56 sites).
- KillThinker (COP #3D): unlink the calling thinker and return its slot to the free list (29 sites).

The spawn handlers copy the caller's animScratch2 ($7F000E,X) into the new thinker and clear its $0E. They do not test AllocateSpecialActor's carry: when the pool is exhausted Y still holds the caller's slot, so the entry-pointer stores would land on the caller (analysis only, unverified at runtime). Handlers return by writing the next script address into the COP stack frame ($02,S) and RTI.
cop_handlers_vram:
Graphics-loading COP handlers (Bank $00): AdhocVramDma (#4F), CopyPalette (#50), Decompress (#51) and SetScratchPointer (#54).

AdhocVramDma stages a one-shot VRAM transfer in the adhoc DMA block ($7F0C03 source word, then adhocVramDmaBank, adhocVramDmaDest, adhocVramDmaSize) and waits for the NMI (DmaAdhocVramBlock) to run it and zero the destination word. It yields by rewinding the actor entry address ($00) to the COP itself, so every call after the first is a poll; extendedFlags bit 0 marks "staged".

CopyPalette copies colors into the cgramPalette staging ($7F0A00) with the RAM block-move stub at $0402 (PHB, MVN, PLB, RTS; written by system_init). Decompress runs QuintetLzDecompress from a ROM source into a WRAM output buffer, then clears the actor render list. SetScratchPointer stores a long pointer in animScratch for the actor's own code.
cop_handlers_wait:
COP wait handlers WaitByte ($DA) and WaitWord ($DB): frame-count delays for actor scripts (44225–44254, Bank 00).

Both load a frame count into the actor's waitCounter ($08), save the resume address (script cursor $0A/$0C → entryPtr $00/$02, i.e. the byte after the operand) and yield with RTL. The actor loop (RunActors_*, actor_execution.asm) runs DEC $08 once per actor tick and resumes the script at entryPtr when the result goes negative, so a count of N resumes N+1 ticks later (0 = next tick).

WaitByte reads a 1-byte count; WaitWord reads a 2-byte count (delays over 255 ticks) and jumps into WaitByte's shared tail, WaitStoreAndYield.

Contrast: JumpAfterDelay continues at a new script address after its delay, and SetEntryHereAndYield yields one tick with no count (both in cop_handlers_script_control).

Three COP commands that fill the world-map state block (see WorldMapController: $0D52–$0D6F) and return; they never change scene themselves. Storing a nonzero X in worldMapStagedX ($0D52) arms the world-map transition: CheckSceneTransition then sends the game to scene $FE and ExecuteSceneTransition moves $0D52 to worldMapPlayerX ($0D54).

- StageWorldMapMove (COP #65): player start X/Y and a route ID to play automatically (13 NPC departure scripts in towns).
- StageWorldMapChoice (COP #66): player start X/Y and a selection ID for the route-choice dispatch (overworld_exit, 27 sites).
- StageWorldMapMoveIds (COP #67): route ID only, used by the world_map_options route handlers (24 sites).

All handlers return by writing the next script address into the COP stack frame ($02,S) and RTI.

diary_menu_window_dma:
Diary-menu highlight-band thinker for scene $FA (Bank 00, 48049-48203; spawned through thinker_spawn_0CEB18, the scene-$FA slot of the scene thinker table).

Every frame it chooses HDMA tables for the PPU window-1 position registers WH0/WH1 ($2126/$2127; the operand #26 of COP QueueHdmaDirect is that B-bus register, see hdma_channel_config) from three cursor words kept by sFA_diary_menu, where a negative value means 'none': $0D92 = slot cursor, $0D96 = copy-target slot, $0D98 = tab / settings-row cursor. DiaryMenuInit sets WOBJSEL = $22 (window 1 is the colour window) and CGWSEL = $82 (main screen black inside it), so each table lays a band over the rows under a cursor; the band appearance is decoded from the registers, not observed (OQ-I057-3).

=== TABLES ===

Each dma-channel entry is one HDMA step: line count, WH0 (left), WH1 (right); the assembler appends the $00 terminator, so an array is 3n + 1 bytes and an empty array is a lone terminator (no band). WH0 = $FF with WH1 = $00 is an empty window (left > right), i.e. no band on those lines.
- No part notes on diary_band_empty / diary_band_slot1 on purpose: the transforms.json rule for this block swaps those two labels with a regex that needs them adjacent, and a note line between them stops it matching (the ROM then loses a byte). diary_band_empty is the empty table (terminator only, no band); diary_band_slot1 is the slot-1 band.
- Slot bands (31 lines tall, x = $10-$F0): diary_band_slot1 starts at line 79 (slot 1), diary_band_slot2 at line 111 (slot 2), diary_band_slot3 at line 143 (slot 3; two empty entries of $10 + $7F lines because one count cannot exceed $7F).
- Tab / row bands (15 lines tall, x = $30-$D0): diary_band_tab0 at line 79, diary_band_tab1 at 95, diary_band_tab2 at 111, diary_band_tab3 at 127. diary_band_empty and diary_band_tab_empty are the empty tables.

=== SELECTION ===

1. Slot cursor $0D92 (first QueueHdmaDirect): negative writes WH0/WH1 = $FF/$00 directly and queues the empty table; 0 / 1 / 2+ queue the slot-1 / slot-2 / slot-3 band. While a copy target is set ($0D96 >= 0) this band is only queued on odd frames (even frames queue the empty table), so the source row flickers at 30 Hz.
2. Target cursor $0D96 (second QueueHdmaDirect): same mapping, always queued.
3. Tab cursor $0D98 (third QueueHdmaDirect): negative = empty table, 0 / 1 / 2 / 3+ = the four narrow bands.
Each COP QueueHdmaDirect takes its own direct-table HDMA channel, so the three tables overlay each other on the same registers.
