EnemyDropSystem:
Enemy drop spawner for gems and heals (Bank 00, 57129-57340). The old names (DarkGemDropSystem, SpawnDarkGemType1 and so on) said 'dark gem', but what drops is a pickup carrying item id $83 to $86 of GiveItemToPlayer: 1, 2 or 5 gems, or a 5 HP heal.

=== CALLER ===

StandardEnemyDefeatHandler reaches EnemyGemDropRouter when the defeated enemy's stat byte +3 (enemy-stats gemDropType) is nonzero and either this scene's reward flag $0300 is set or enemies remain (the last enemy of a scene whose reward is still unclaimed gets the stat reward instead of a gem). The router spawns one of three entries with SpawnListAppend (flags $0420, so the pickup inherits the dead enemy's position through CopyActorState): value 1 = SpawnDropGem1 (fixed $83), value 2 = SpawnDropGem2 (fixed $84), any other nonzero value (3) = SpawnDropByHpTier (random, see below).

=== THE PICKUP ===

The actor carries its item id in chatPtr ($7F000A,X) and has the 'friendly' flag $0020 in its $10 (from the spawn flags). When the player overlaps it, combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr) and turns the actor into NpcDespawnStub. Ids: $83 = 1 gem, $84 = 2 gems, $85 = 5 gems (cap 999), $86 = hpToHeal += 5 (UpdateHUD refills 1 HP every 8 frames) plus the spark effect and SFX $22.
Each entry also spawns a marked child, interaction_handlers.collect_handler_gem (flags $2700), which pulls the pickup toward the player while L / R is held. The pickup is the marked parent ($12 bit $0040 set by SpawnAfterMarked), so its Die also removes the child. Each body clears $10 bit $0400 that the $0420 spawn flags set (see OQ-I049-3).

=== LIFETIME (spriteset_pickups_effects animation lists) ===

Gems: anim 4 / 5 / 6 (gems $83 / $84 / $85) for 10 passes (about 75 ticks each: a 60-tick still frame and 5 shimmer frames of 3 ticks, about 750 ticks), then the blink anim 9 / $0A / $0B for 150 passes (2 ticks each, about 300 ticks), then Die. Heal: anim $22 for 180 passes (2 ticks, about 360 ticks), then anim $35 for 60 passes (4 ticks, about 240 ticks), then Die.

=== WEIGHTED DROP (SpawnDropByHpTier) ===

HP tier by the player's HP against max HP: HP <= max/4 uses table group $20, HP <= max/2 uses group $10, otherwise group 0. A random byte is compared against the group's four ascending thresholds (the last is $0100, so it always matches) and the first row whose threshold is above the byte gives the body to run. Probabilities of 256 outcomes:
HP above half: $86 heal 5.9%, $85 5 gems 17.6%, $84 2 gems 36.3%, $83 1 gem 40.2%. HP between a quarter and a half: $85 9.8%, $83 19.9%, $86 30.1%, $84 40.2%. HP at or below a quarter: $84 4.7%, $83 15.2%, $85 29.7%, $86 50.4%. The heal becomes the likeliest drop when the player is low on HP.
EscortFollowPathTracker:
Escort follower actor (Bank 00, 51206-51522; the delta table follows): spawned as a child of an escort NPC (Kara / Lily), it records the player's path and replays it on the NPC, so the NPC walks the player's route about 8 recorded frames behind.

=== SPAWN AND PARAMETERS ===

SpawnAfterFlags ( EscortFollowPathTracker, #$2000 ) (#$2800 in btDE_kara_missing) in ec0A_kara, it1A_lily, ir1C_lily, eu97_clerk2, btDF_kara, btDE_kara_missing and btE3_kara. The child sits right behind its parent in the actor list, so its $04 (prevActorLink) is the NPC. The spawner sets orbitAngle = initial facing + 1 (Lily: 4, so facing 3) or 0 (use the player's current facing), and orbitDiameter = the NPC's base animation index (Lily: $1A).

=== RING BUFFER at $7EDF00 ===

Eight-byte entries: X word, Y word, facing word, unused. The setup writes 9 entries (offsets $00-$40): a trail that starts at the NPC and steps 2 px per entry along the table row of the facing index. The row is the OPPOSITE direction and the entry's facing word the opposite facing (EscortFollowPathDeltaTable: facing 0 South steps Y -2, 1 North Y +2, 2 West X +2, 3 East X -2). Only 8 entries are ever read: every access masks orbitAngle with $3F, so the byte offset runs $00-$38 and the ninth entry ($7EDF40) is unreachable. No other code uses $7EDF00.

=== PER FRAME (after SetEntryHereAndYield) ===

Own $14 / $16 = the player's position of the last frame, $0E = the facing last applied to the NPC, orbitAngle = ring head (byte offset).
- Player moved: the NPC jumps to the head entry (written 8 recorded frames ago), the head entry is overwritten with the player's current X / Y, and when the head entry's facing differs from $0E the NPC gets animation orbitDiameter + facing + 4 ($28; $2A and $08 cleared). Then the head entry's facing is refreshed with the player's current facing and the head advances by 8.
- Player still: the NPC shows animation orbitDiameter + facing of the head entry (no +4); its position is untouched, the head does not advance and $0E := $FFFF so the next move restarts the walk animation.

Edge: GetPlayerFacingDirection returns carry set and A >= 4 for an unknown facing; the table index then runs past the four rows (OQ-I052-7). The old header said '9-waypoint ring buffer' and 'each frame advances orbitAngle by 8'; the head advances only on frames where the player moved, and the first use of orbitAngle is a seed, not a timer.

- $26 nonzero, or the room's clear reward already taken (TestFlag_0300(sceneCurrent) set), or tier 0: FieldRevealFromActorStats reads the byte at +3 of the spawner's stat table. & 3 = 0 dies at once; 1 / 2 / 3 = a gem pickup with anim $04 / $05 / $06 and item $83 / $84 / $85 (1 / 2 / 5 gems, given by GiveItemToPlayer).

FieldRevealDrop stores the item id in chatPtr ($7F000A), remembers the spawn Y in $24 and sets $26 := 7 (the step budget). With Y aligned to a 16 px row it probes the tile with BranchIfSolidHere: while the tile is solid it moves one row (16 px) down, at most 8 rows, and stops early on a tile whose collision byte is $0E; after 8 failures the target is the spawn Y + 1. The target goes to moveXAlt / moveYAlt, the actor returns to its spawn Y, flies to the target (MoveToward, 4 px per frame), hops once (Y chain $45: -2, -2, -1, -1, 0, 0, +1, +1, +2, +2), waits 12 ticks (WaitByte #0B) and spawns collect_handler_gem (SpawnAfterMarked #$2300): holding L / R then pulls the pickup toward the player.
It then animates in 100-frame blocks. A stat item (anim $0C-$0E, at least 8) repeats forever. A gem (anim $04-$06) switches to anim + 5 after the first block (the blink animations $09 / $0A / $0B, inferred: OQ-I051-7), plays 10 more frames and falls into FieldRevealDieEmpty (Die): a gem lives about 110 frames.

The old header said it checks that all enemies are cleared and stages HP / STR / DEF gem sprites. The flag means 'this room's reward is already taken', and only the tier path stages stat items; the gem path stages gems.

flag_helpers:
Event-flag and WRAM-flag bit helpers (Bank $00).

All flags live in one bit array starting at eventFlags ($0A00): flag N is bit (N AND 7) of byte $0A00 + N÷8 (masks from bitmasks_bit_position). Flag indices are 16-bit. The helper names carry the base that is added to the index in A:
  $0000 (…Raw: TestFlagRaw/SetFlagRaw/ClearFlagRaw) — bytes $0A00–$0A1F; the index is masked to a byte
  $0100 (…_0100) — bytes $0A20–$0A3F, event/trigger flags: StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, EnemyDefeatDispatch and some boss/puzzle actors; this is the 32-byte field that event_blocks.ApplyAllEventBlocks scans, so flag $0100+n triggers event block n
  $0200 (…_0200) — bytes $0A40–$0A5F, persistent world events: chests opened (byte 3 of scene_chest_table records) and hidden Red Jewels
  $0300 (…_0300) — bytes $0A60–$0A7F, one flag per scene ID: the scene's clear reward has been claimed (radar, StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, boss_clear_reward_handler)
  $0400 (SetWramFlag/TestWramFlag) — bytes $0A80–$0A9F = wramFlags, 256 flags indexed by enemy number (SetDungeonKillFlag, CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag); ClearAllWramFlags zero-fills exactly this block
  $0500 (TestWramFlag_Offset100/SetWramFlag_Offset100 with index 0–7, and TestFlag_0510) — bytes $0AA0 and up: boss reward flags $0500–$0507 and ability unlock flags $0510+ (TestAbilityFlag: characterForm×4 + slot)

wramFlags is therefore just the $0400–$04FF slice of the event flag array, accessed with its own base. ClearAllWramFlags is called only by WorldMapController (on entering the world map) and by the scripts st68_kara and sp58_red_eye, and game_over_sequence clears the same block inline on a true death; no reset at ordinary scene changes was found, so these flags outlive a single scene (OQ-67). The _Offset100 variants add $0100 to the index and so land at $0AA0, outside the cleared block (OQ-68).

Calling convention: the flag index is in A (16-bit); the core routines (SetEventFlag, ClearEventFlag, TestEventFlag, SetWramFlag, TestWramFlag) are JSR-only, preserve X, clobber Y and WRAM scratch $0000, and the Test routines return carry = flag set and A = the isolated bit. The JSL wrappers add the base and call the cores. TestWramFlag has no caller outside this file (CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag in actor_execution repeats the logic inline with its own BitMaskTable_Wram).

Cutscene auto-walk actors (Bank 00) spawned by warps_interaction.StartForcedWalk during extended warp transitions.

StartForcedWalk decodes the direction from scrollStepTableBase (bit 5 = west, bit 4 = east, bit 7 = north, default south), sets playerFlags $0100 and spawns the matching ForcedWalkSouth/North/West/East on the player actor (SpawnBefore).

The warp entry gives two things: the walk-step stream pointed to by warpFacing ($0650, a pointer to warp entry +7) and the walk sequence index in scrollStepTableBase. Stream layout, 6 bytes: [direction byte][X offset word][Y offset word][direction byte]. A direction byte indexes walk_step_table, whose entry is (animation index, index into move_chain_table); move_chain_table entries are delta-node lists, so ReadDirSprite_*Velocity leaves a velocity-curve pointer in $2E (Y) or $2C (X).

Each ForcedWalk* actor: masks all joypad input, reads the first direction byte, stages the player sprite (StagePlayerSprFromDP, animation index from DP $0000), replaces scrollStepTableBase with the pointer to the word scroll-step list from forced_walk_pan_table (read by CameraScrollStepLookup, ends at a zero word), pans the camera in the walk direction (CameraPan*), adds the stream's X/Y offset words to its own position (ApplyScrollOffset), reads the second direction byte, stages the final sprite, copies position and state to the player (SyncPlayerToCamera), unmasks the joypad and dies.

The direction variants differ only in the ReadDirSprite helper (Y velocity for south/north, X for west/east) and the CameraPan* COP.

game_over_sequence:
Player death sequence (Bank 00, 54831-55263) with its helper actors. combat_collision.CheckPlayerDeath sets playerFlags $0200 when playerHp is zero, replaces the player actor's entry point with GameOverSequence and calls StopPlayerOnDeath, so the player actor itself runs this script from the next tick. Entry points: GameOverSequence (player), GameOverCutsceneSprites (spawned by it), GameOverSparkleOrbitA/B (spawned by that) and DeathWakeupMessage (spawned by player_character after the respawn).

=== TIMELINE ===

Frame 0: player $10 |= $0040 (dead; shadow_shimmer reads it) and joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button and the D-pad, Start and Select included).
After 33 ticks (WaitByte #20): spawn DeathPaletteFadeThinker (palette bundles $10, then $0E) and GameOverCutsceneSprites (the sparkles).
After 120 more ticks (WaitByte #77): clear player $10 bit $8000 (the player stops using DecomposePlayerSprites), SFX $0C on both channels (the same SFX as the Dark Space warp) and play animation #1C of spriteset_pickups_effects once (also used by the Dark Space warp).
Fade: orbitAngle starts at 15; every pass writes counter - 1 to INIDISP (brightness 14 down to 0) and waits 4 ticks (WaitByte #03), 60 ticks in all. Forced blank is never set.
Then two one-frame palette thinkers (PaletteResetAndKillThinker with bundle IDs $0B and $0D: sub-entry 0 of each bundle is applied once), one yield and the respawn choice.

=== RESPAWN CHOICE ===

gemCount >= 100 (revive): gemCount -= 100, playerHp = playerMaxHp >> 1, and the respawn record is the one stored by the last warp the player took (reviveWarpPtr / reviveWarpBank, $0AF4 / $0AF6; ExecuteWarp writes a pointer to entry + 4 for every warp). Form and wramFlags are kept.
gemCount < 100 (real game over): gemCount = 0, characterForm = 0 (Will), or 2 (Shadow) when sceneCurrent is $E8 (the Dark Gaia arena in the comet lair; presumably because that fight is played as Shadow), playerHp = playerMaxHp, the 16 words of wramFlags ($0A80-$0A9F: dungeon kill and puzzle flags) are cleared, and the respawn record is sceneSaveData / sceneSaveDataBank ($0AF0 / $0AF2), which ExecuteWarp writes only for warps whose entry byte 9 has bit 7 set.

=== SHARED RESPAWN TAIL ===

Reads the warp record at DBR:Y: byte 0 = scene (sceneNext, 8-bit store), +1 and +3 = spawn X and Y (warpDestX / warpDestY), +5 = facing with bit 7 masked (warpFacing), +6 = packed camera window (warpScrollParams). Then gfxCacheIdxB := $0404, gameOverWakeupFlag += 1, worldReadyFlag := 0 (ExecuteSceneTransition then skips the exit transition, because the screen is already black, and runs the enter transition) and SetEntryHere + RTL; the scene change takes over.

=== WAKE-UP MESSAGE ===

player_character spawns DeathWakeupMessage (SpawnAfterFlags $2000) at the start of the next scene when gameOverWakeupFlag ($0AF8) is set. It masks the joypad with $CFFC (Select and Start stay live), clears the flag, waits 3 ticks (WaitByte #02), prints one of three strings chosen by characterForm (0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow), unmasks and dies. The message follows a revive as well as a real game over. After a real game over the form is Will (Shadow in $E8), so the Freedan line appears only after a revive as Freedan.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The ROM masks the joypad with $FFF0 (and $CFF0 in DeathWakeupMessage); db-us/transforms.json (block game_over_sequence) widens both to $FFFC / $CFFC so the software-only buttons $0004 and $0008 are masked too, and the extracted asm shows the transformed values. The old comment credited the first block with spawning both helpers (it is a 33-tick wait first); 'sound #$0C' is the 16-bit pair $0C0C on both channels. The old header did not say that 100 gems are paid in the revive case, that the wramFlags are cleared only on a real game over, or that two different warp records are used.

global_ambient_dispatcher:
Per-scene hub thinker (Bank 00, 49035-49577, about 545 bytes), spawned in about 60 scene_thinkers lists, usually as the last slot. It has two jobs: it loads the player's sprite palette for the current form once at spawn, and it runs the shared 'talk to the thing in front of you' interaction every frame. It is not an ambient effect, and the trigger is the interact bit of joypadCurrent, not a direction press as the old header said.

=== PALETTE (spawn only) ===

SwitchCase on characterForm ($0AD4: 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow; no range check, so the table's fourth entry is never reached) runs PaletteStart / PaletteStep on bundle #0B (Will), #0C (Freedan) or #23 (Shadow). All three write colours $81-$8F, which is OBJ palette 0 colours 1-15, the player's sprite palette. #0B and #0C are a single static strip; #23 is an animated set of strips (wait 2 each). PaletteStep plays the whole bundle before the script continues. The palette is chosen once when the thinker spawns, so a form change in the middle of a scene is not re-applied until the next scene setup.

=== FILTER WORD ===

thinker-def <#00, #08> gives animScratch2 = $0800 (bit 11 set: also run in the Light runners). GlobalAmbientInteractEntry clears bit 11 in the thinker's own animScratch2, so from then on the dispatcher runs only in RunThinkers_General (the main loop) and is skipped by the lighter frame routines (dialogue, render, music upload): no new talk starts while a dialogue frame loop is running. The old comment called bit 11 an 'interaction ready flag'.

=== TALK INTERACTION (every frame) ===

1. PHD / TCD set D = 0 and joypadCurrent bit $8000 is tested: the interact bit. In the vanilla layout it is the B button (remapB); in this build transforms.json rewrites the system_init defaults to remapA = $8080 and remapB = $4008, so the A button feeds it (together with the attack bit $0080). The notes in this file name the logical bit, not a button. Not pressed: return.
2. GetPlayerFacingDirection: carry SET = no valid facing, return; carry CLEAR = valid (GlobalAmbientFacingValid; the old label said Invalid). A = 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right, saved in $09EE.
3. A probe point one pixel in front of the player ($18 / $1C = player X / Y plus (0,+1), (0,-1), (-1,0) or (+1,0)) is built. The four probe labels follow the facing code: GlobalAmbientProbeDown handles facing 0 (down), GlobalAmbientProbeUp facing 1 (up), GlobalAmbientProbeLeft facing 2 (left), GlobalAmbientProbeRight facing 3 (right); the old ScanEast / ScanWest / ScanNorth / ScanSouth labels were rotated against these.
4. GlobalAmbientFindActorInFront walks the actor list from actorListFirst and keeps the actor with the smallest |dx| + |dy| to the probe point whose |dx| and |dy| are both below $10 and whose sum is below $20. Only actors with Flags10 bit $1000 count (the third actor-def header byte of NPCs and objects carries it; the player has it clear and is skipped). X = 0 when none is found.
5. The target is 'in front' when its coordinate along the facing axis is beyond the probe (GlobalAmbientTargetInRange), otherwise it is at or behind the player (GlobalAmbientTargetAtOrBehind). Both need a non-zero chatPtr ($7F000A, set by SetInteractHandler). A target at or behind the player runs its chat routine directly; a target in front first sets the interact bit in joypadHeld.
6. In front and Flags12 ($12) bit $0200 clear: the turn-and-talk path (GlobalAmbientTalkWithSnapshot; it plays no sound, which the old label TalkSound suggested). The target's actor slot ($30 bytes, bank 0) and its extended $7F page ($30 bytes) are copied to $7E:3410-$346F through the RAM MVN stub at $0402 ($0404 = destination bank, $0405 = source bank, A = $2F is the byte count minus one, not a sound number; the old comments called it SFX $2F). The target is then turned to face the player (GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame), its animation is updated at once, its chat routine runs as a subroutine and, when it returns, both copies are written back (GlobalAmbientTalkRestoreActor). WRAM flags, dialogue and inventory changes made by the chat routine persist, but the NPC's own actor fields (position, animation, entry pointer, flags) are put back as they were; the next-link $06 is kept as it is now when the saved copy had none (it was the list tail).

hit_stagger_controller:
Hit knockback and recovery controller (Bank 00, 55415-55927). One short-lived actor is spawned per hit. It slides the victim along one axis for 16 frames by moving ITSELF (collision-checked movement) and copying its position to the victim every frame, then either hands control back (player) or resolves the hit (enemy: HP check, hit / death callback). It has no sprite and is never placed by a scene.

=== SPAWN CONTRACT ===

Four spawn sites: ApplyPlayerHitstun and combat_collision.ApplyInteractionDamage (flags word $2400, victim = the player) and the two enemy-hit paths in combat_collision (flags $2000). The flags word becomes the child's $10: $2000 = script-driven run path (own wait counter; actor_execution moves such an actor only while $12 bit 3 is set), $0400 = 'the victim is the player': the controller tests it to choose HitStaggerReleasePlayer instead of HitStaggerResolveHit (the old note said $0400 marks an enemy and that the old label HitStaggerReturnAI 're-enables AI for enemies'; HitStaggerReleasePlayer only ever handles the player). CopyActorState gives the child the victim's position, anim index, $12 (without $1000) and, in $24, the victim's slot. The spawner then stores a direction code in the child's $28 and zeroes its $2C / $2E, and copies the victim's extendedFlags bit $0020 ('hitstun skip' in the WRAM map) into the child.
Direction code in $28: 0 = south, 1 = north, 2 = west, 3 = east (CalcKnockbackDirection), 4 or more = no knockback. free101C ($7F101C) of the victim is a knockback TIER: 0 for ordinary actors, 1 for the player (player_character init) and mu5F_cyclops; the only writers in extracted/ are CopyActorState (zero), those three and this file (copy to the child).

=== HitStaggerMain ===

$10 |= $0008 (collision-checked movement) unless the victim has extendedFlags $0020; $12 |= $0008 (movement request for a script-driven actor). If $12 bit $0010 is set (inherited from the victim: stagger-immune in combat_collision) or the direction code is 4 or more, there is no knockback: WaitByte #$0F (16 ticks), then HitStaggerReleasePlayer (player) or HitStaggerResolveHit. Otherwise the victim's pixel X / Y are saved in orbitAngle / orbitDiameter ($7F0010 / $7F0012: no orbit here, the words are reused as the START position), the tier is copied, and the direction code is decoded by chained DEC / BMI (the old note spoke of a '3-deep stack-encoded direction index'; there is no such stack): 0 = Y chain (carry set), 1 = Y chain with SetMoveNegateXY (negated), 2 = X chain with SetMoveNegateXY, 3 = X chain (carry clear). Each branch first clears the inherited ForceDir bits ($6000 of $12). The branches JSR HitStaggerApplyKnockbackDelta, which pushes HitStaggerStoreMovementDelta as a return address; that routine stores the movement chain head in $2E (carry set, $26 := 0, vertical) or $2C (carry clear, $26 := 1, horizontal; the old doc had the axis flag the other way round). The RTS chain ends in HitStaggerSlideLoop (pushed by Main).
Curves (move_chain_table, one delta per frame, pixels): tier 0 uses entry $22 = 4 4 5 5 5 5 4 4 3 3 2 2 1 1 0 (sum 48 px = 3 tiles); tier 1 and above use entry $23 = 3 3 4 4 3 3 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 0 (sum 32 px = 2 tiles). The player is tier 1.

=== HitStaggerSlideLoop (the 16-frame slide loop) ===

SetEntryHereAndYield, then LoopStart #$10: 16 frames in which the child's $14 / $16 are copied into the victim. After the loop: the player ($10 bit $0400) goes to HitStaggerReleasePlayer. An enemy without $10 bit $0008 goes straight to ResolveHit. Otherwise the distance travelled along the axis ($26 = 0: Y, else X) is d = |start - current|: d = 0 resolves at once; if d is a multiple of 16 HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance compares it with the tier threshold (tier 0 $30, tier 1 $20, tier 2 and above $40) and carry CLEAR (equal = the full slide happened) resolves; any other d is a CUT-SHORT slide (a wall stopped it): the victim's chain pointer and delta word on the knocked axis are zeroed ($2E and $7F002E for a vertical slide, $2C and $7F002C for a horizontal one) and its wait counter $08 is zeroed when it has no chain on the other axis, so its script resumes immediately (purpose inferred, OQ-I046-3). The thresholds equal the curve sums (48 and 32), which is why a full slide matches exactly; tiers 2 and 3 use the 32-px curve with a $40 threshold and could never match (no actor uses them).

=== HitStaggerResolveHit (enemy) ===

HP ($7F0026) nonzero: if onHitCallback ($7F1000) is set it becomes the victim's entry address (low word only, the bank word is unchanged) and is cleared; the victim's iframe counter becomes $FFF4 (-12, recovery). HP zero: the victim's $10 gets $0040 (dead) unless it already has it, its entry becomes onDeathCallback / onDeathCallbackBank when set (and $08, $2C, $2E are zeroed) or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler in the same bank. Finally X := D (the child) and COP Die, because the COP needs X = the actor slot.

=== HitStaggerReleasePlayer (player only) ===

Unless playerFlags has $0A00 (game over / script lock) the player's entry address becomes player_character.PlayerIdleEntry. The player's iframe counter is set to $FFE2 (-30) and the D-pad bits $0F00 of joypadMaskStd are cleared (shown again). Because a positive counter freezes the player controller, overwriting the $003C that ApplyPlayerHitstun wrote ends the stun after the 16-frame slide (about 17 ticks), not after 60; a heavy hit's -60 is likewise shortened to -30.

=== Helpers ===

HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance stores d in the absolute scratch $0000 and pushes HitStaggerZeroToCarry - 1, so the CMP's RTS lands in HitStaggerZeroToCarry, which turns Z into carry (CLC when equal, SEC otherwise). All operands written with four hex digits ($0000, $002C, $002E, $0008 ...) are absolute addresses; $0000 is the global scratch word, the others are the slot fields indexed by X.

Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); the arithmetic and flow are read from the code and the move_chain_table nodes.

Hit switch (Bank 00, 51710-51778; formerly named floor_button): a solid, hit-triggered switch that raises one numbered event flag each time it is struck. It is not a pressure plate: the actor is solid (MarkSolidHere), so the player cannot stand on it, and the trigger is the engine's hit callback. The old text ('triggers puzzle state when the player or objects land on the plate', 'used in pyramid puzzle rooms') is wrong.

=== INIT ===

combat_collision dispatches onHitCallback ($7F1000) after the hit damage: the callback pointer becomes the victim's entry address and onHitCallback is cleared, so the script below runs on the actor's next turn. HitSwitchTriggered: SetFlagRaw with A = $24 (the event-flag number, no base offset), frame $10 (assumed to be the pressed look; not viewed), AnimOnce, WaitByte #0F (16 ticks), frame $0F, AnimOnce, then BRA HitSwitchRearm which restores HP $FF and registers the callback again. The button can therefore be struck again after about 16 ticks plus two animation cycles.

The gw85 actors run WaitOnFlagByte ( #n, #01 ) followed by ClearFlagByte ( #n ), so in the rampway the flag is a one-shot trigger consumed by the gate or spear. gw83_switch waits on flag $01 and does not clear it. In scene 87 the flag $0F has no waiter among the scene's actors (the gw82_wall_spear actors it spawns use timers only); $0F is also used as an unrelated flag in Babel Tower and Freejia scripts (OQ-I042-3).

interaction_handlers:
Runtime pull / collect interaction handlers (Bank 00): three small actor scripts spawned with SpawnAfterMarked as children of a gem or a movable solid (collect_handler_gem, push_handler_solid, push_handler_forceball).

The child's $04 (prevActorLink) is the actor it was marked after, i.e. the object being moved (the 'parent'). The handler reads the player position ($0014 / $0016 of playerActor) and edits the parent's posX / posY ($14 / $16). Its own $14 / $16 start as a copy of the parent's (CopyActorState) and are used as the reference position for every distance test.

=== SHARED STRUCTURE ===

1. SetSavedPtr( &self ) keeps the idle entry in retPtr1 ($7F0004). RestoreSavedPtr later resumes there (and clears retPtr1), which re-arms the handler. Every 'Restore' label below is that exit.
2. SetEntryHereAndYield + BranchIfPressed( #$0031 ): bit 0 of the mask selects joypadRaw, and $0030 is the L / R shoulder pair (the guard / channel button; player_character BlockStopToIdle tests the same $0030 for 'L/R released'). Not held: RTL, poll again next frame.
3. BranchIfPlayerNear( #0F ): radius 15 tiles, a square |dx| and |dy| < 241 px. A coarse gate only.
4. BranchOnPlayerX( #$000F, ... ): the engine handler (cop_handlers_player_query) loads operand slot +2 when the player is more than 15 px WEST of the actor, +6 when more than 15 px EAST and +4 when within 15 px (including 0). The slot +4 operand is therefore 'player in the same column', and in this file it leads to the block that works on the Y axis ($0016, posY). BranchOnPlayerY does the same for the row and leads to the blocks that work on posX ($0014).
   (docs/cop/families/player_query.md and the copdef label the three operands West / East / Here, but the handler's order is West / Here / East; see OQ-I037-3.)
5. Each axis block computes d = player - own position. d < 0 means the player is above (Y blocks) or west of (X blocks) the object. |d| is needed, then GetPlayerFacingDirection must report that the player faces the object (codes 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right), then the object is moved ONE direction: toward the player. These handlers therefore pull the object to the player; the 'push' in the old names and header was a guess.
6. The label pairs are named after the wrong axis: *AlignWest / *MoveWest and *AlignEast / *MoveEast are the vertical blocks (player above / below), *AlignNorth / *MoveNorth and *AlignSouth / *MoveSouth are the horizontal ones (player west / east). Each block's second BPL after the first BPL is dead (N is still set), so the abs() always runs for d < 0.

=== HANDLERS ===

collect_handler_gem: no clearance test and no collision painting. Step count = |d| / 2 (kept in orbitAngle, $7F0010,X). After the first facing test it SetEntryHere's, so the following frames skip the button / facing tests and move the parent 2 px per frame (parent posY / posX -/+ 2, own copy updated too) until the count reaches zero, then restore idle. The old header said it nudges the player; it moves the parent (the gem) and only reads the player.
push_handler_solid: needs |d| >= $20 (32 px), BranchIfSolidOffset( dx, dy ) one tile toward the player clear (any lower-nibble bit set = blocked), ClearSolidHere, own pos -/+ $10, MarkSolidHere (collision moves at once), SFX $2C, then parent $12 bit $0010 is set (old state kept in $24) while LoopStart( $10 ) slides the parent 1 px per pass (16 passes = one tile), then the bit is restored. $12 bit $0010 is damage / stagger immunity in combat_collision (the wram map calls it push-in-progress). The check state skips a frame when the parent's $10 bit $0080 (victim iframe flag) is set and $12 bit $0010 is clear.
push_handler_forceball: same distance and facing tests, but additionally the player's sprite index ($28) must be $3A (player above the ball), $3B (below), $3D (west) or $3C (east), the poses that match down / up / left / right. It uses NudgePosition( dx, dy ) on its own position instead of Clear / MarkSolidHere, and while the button is not held it copies the parent's posX / posY every frame.

=== SPAWN BYTES = VELOCITY (the first two actors) ===

InitActorFromSceneData turns the record's X and Y bytes into pixels (byte x 16), so $14 >> 4 gives the X byte back and $16 >> 4 the Y byte. Both are decoded as sign-magnitude: bit 7 = negative, bits 0-6 = magnitude. The Y byte is decremented first, so Y byte 1 = 0, 2 = +1, $82 = -1; Y byte 0 gives $0081 (+129), a quirk the shipped records never use. Result: Layer1DriftWrapped drifts at X +1, Y -1 px per frame; Layer1DriftUnbounded at X +2, Y +1.

npc_wander_ai:
Reusable town-NPC wander behaviour (Bank 00, 50968-51193) used by 13 ambient NPC actors in Dao (daC9_businessman, daC3_man1), Watermia (wa78 water_kid, moving_woman, glass_game, centipede_man), Angel Village (av6B villagers2, ocean_ache), Euro (eu91 women2, men2), Seaside Palace (sp5A_villagers) and South Cape (sc01_roof_man, sc04_poverty).

=== CALLING PATTERN ===

The NPC's init stores its base animation index in currentHp,X ($7F0026) and calls SyncActorPosFromDP once. Its loop is: JSL NpcRandomWanderAI, SetEntryHereAndYield, SetEntryHere, AnimOnce, BRA loop. The routines here only choose and stage; the caller's AnimOnce plays the staged animation.

=== DATA ===

$7F0010 / $7F0012 (mnemonics orbitAngle / orbitDiameter, there is no orbit here) hold the home X / Y that SyncActorPosFromDP copies from DP $14 / $16. $7F0026 (mnemonic currentHp) is the NPC's base animation index. The sprite sheet is laid out as base + 0 to 3 = stand south / north / west / east and base + 4 to 7 = walk south / north / west / east.

=== DECISION ===

NpcRandomWanderAI rolls RngByte and 7 (each case has probability 1/8) and runs COP SwitchCase on the byte at $0000. The table is: 0 = stand north, 1 = stand south, 2 = stand west, 3 = stand east, 4 = step north, 5 = step south, 6 = step west, 7 = step east (the old note listed cases 4 to 7 as south / north / west / east; cases 4 and 5 are north and south, and cases 0 and 1 are the stand pair north and south).
Standing: $28 := base + direction, $2A := 0, UpdateActorAnimation, $08 := $78 (the script sleeps 121 ticks after the caller's SetEntryHereAndYield: $78 skipped passes, then it runs on the next one) and MarkSolidHere (a standing NPC blocks the player).
Stepping: if the NPC is already more than $30 pixels (3 tiles) from its home in that direction, or the BranchIfSolid test for that side finds a solid tile, it stands facing that direction instead. Otherwise it stages a movement delta chain (StageMoveX / StageMoveY #$11 = +1 pixel every second frame, east or south; #$12 = -1 every second frame, west or north), sets the walk animation (base + 4 to 7), and does ClearSolidHere (a walking NPC is not solid).
The step lasts for one pass of the walk animation: the caller's AnimOnce moves the NPC at half a pixel per frame until the animation list ends, then clears the chain ($2C / $2E) and the loop rolls again. The step length is therefore half the number of frames of the walk animation, in pixels, and there is no re-roll in the middle of a step (the old note said 'one-tile forced move').

Exit-to-world-map actor (Bank 00, 51781-52569). One copy is placed in each of 15 town, village and dungeon-entrance scenes (spawn record x 00, y 01, type 00). It waits for the player to reach a fixed exit zone, then stages the world-map arrival position and a destination-menu id and lets the engine switch to the world map.

=== FLOW ===

1. OverworldExitDispatch compares sceneCurrent with 15 scene ids and JMPs to the region handler. The handler tests the exit zone every frame (South Cape re-enters its own handler with SetEntryHere; all other regions go through the compare chain again each frame).
2. Zone tests: a pixel test on playerYPos (South Cape: Y < $10, Edward's Castle: Y == $2D0) or COP BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles ( minX, minY, maxX, maxY ). The tile test runs on (player X, player Y - 8) and is strict at the minimum edge and inclusive at the maximum edge, in tiles x 16.
3. Inside the zone the handler may test story flags with BranchOnFlagByte. The first flag found set wins, so the later-story flag is tested first where there are two.
4. Every success path does the same: $0D60 := 0, COP StageWorldMapChoice ( start X, start Y, choice id ), JMP OverworldExitFinalize. StageWorldMapChoice only writes worldMapStagedX/PlayerY/ChoiceId; a nonzero staged X makes CheckSceneTransition send the game to scene $FE (the world map). WorldMapController then drops the player at the staged position and runs world_map_options[choice] (a 'Quit / destination' menu).
5. OverworldExitFinalize sets gfxCacheIdxB := $0400, SetEntryHere and RTL: the actor then idles at the RTL until the scene changes.

ramps:
Four ramp-jump launcher actors (ramp_east, ramp_west, ramp_north, ramp_south; Bank 00, 53971-54829). Each one watches the player; when the player runs into its window the ramp takes the player's script over, locks the controls and carries the player a fixed distance along one axis. East/west ramps spawn a child actor that adds a precomputed vertical arc, so the player leaps; north/south ramps just move the player vertically for a number of animation cycles. Earlier notes called them collision tiles; they are actors placed through scene_actors.

=== PER-FRAME WATCH (two stages) ===

All four are actor-def <#00,#00,#20> and follow one pattern, mirrored per direction:
1. Stage 1 (every frame): RampCheckPlayerSpeed passes when |speed| on the ramp's axis (playerSpeedEw for east/west, playerSpeedNs for north/south) is at least 6 and playerFlags bit $0800 (script lock) is clear. Then the player must be inside the ramp's window (table below). When both hold the ramp executes SetEntryHere and enters stage 2.
2. Stage 2: every frame the ramp compares the player's position on the ramp's axis with its own. When the two are EXACTLY equal it fires the launch. If the distance grows to $10 or more it goes back to stage 1 with JumpNextFrame. Speed and lock are not rechecked in stage 2.

| Ramp | Axis | Window (player minus ramp) | Direction of the climb | Exit speed |
|------|------|----------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| ramp_east  | X, |dy| <= $18 | +2 .. +15 (player just east) | west (-8 per frame) | $FFF8 |
| ramp_west  | X, |dy| <= $18 | -16 .. -2 (player just west) | east (+8 per frame) | $0008 |
| ramp_north | Y, |dx| <= $10 | +2 .. +15 (player just south) | north (-8 per frame) | $FFF8 on playerSpeedNs |
| ramp_south | Y, |dx| <= $10 | -16 .. -2 (player just north) | south (+8 per frame) | $0008 on playerSpeedNs |

The direction of the speed is not tested: any |speed| >= 6 on the axis arms the ramp. The names describe the side the ramp sits on relative to the player. Chain $10 / $0F of move_chain_table are the constant -8 / +8 per frame movements used by StagePlayerMoveXY. The ramp keeps its temporary window edge in the global words $0018 (east/west) and $001C (south) rather than in its own direct page; nothing yields between writing and using them.

=== LAUNCH (RampBeginPlayerControl) ===

The ramp writes the climb routine's address into the player's entry pointer ($00 / $02 of playerActor), then calls RampBeginPlayerControl: it zeroes playerSpeedEw and playerSpeedNs, stores the ramp's own $0E (the spawn-record type byte >> 1) into the player's statsPtr, zeroes the player's $2C / $2E, masks the D-pad ($0F00 into joypadMaskStd) and sets playerFlags $0800. The ramp itself then restarts at stage 1 and stays blocked by the $0800 lock until RestorePlayerControl clears it. The $0E value is the ramp's parameter: the arc selector for east/west and the loop count for north/south.

=== EAST / WEST CLIMB (RampPlayerClimbEast, RampPlayerClimbWest) ===

Runs as the player. COP [SpawnAfter] RampArcDriver creates the arc child right after the player (the child's $04 link is the player, the player's $06 link is the child); the player then writes the exit speed ($FFF8 east ramp, $0008 west ramp) into the child's orbitDiameter, clears $0008 in its own $10 (collision-aware movement off) and sets $0200, and loops StagePlayerMoveXY plus AnimOnce forever: animation $21 with X chain $10 (-8 per frame) for east, animation $24 with chain $0F (+8) for west. The loop ends because the child restores the player's entry.
RampArcDriver reads the player's statsPtr (0 or 1), multiplies by 3 to index ramp_motion_curves (pointer + frame count), and from then on adds one sign-extended byte of the chosen curve to the player's Y ($16) each frame (ramp_motion_curve_step). After the last frame it copies orbitDiameter into playerSpeedEw, calls slider_glide.RestorePlayerControl, sets slopeStepCounter = 0 and decelStepCounter = 7 and dies.
Spawn type byte 1 ($0E = 0) selects ramp_curve_arc_64: 64 frames, rising up to 204 pixels (peak at frame 28) and returning to the start height (sum 0), about 512 pixels of horizontal travel. Spawn type 3 ($0E = 1) selects ramp_curve_arc_32: 32 frames, peak rise 50 pixels, ending 8 pixels lower (sum +8), about 256 pixels of travel. Only the Itory ramp pair (scene 15) uses type 1; every other east/west ramp uses type 3. These distances are static estimates (8 px x frames); they were not measured at runtime.

=== NORTH / SOUTH CLIMB (RampPlayerClimbNorth, RampPlayerClimbSouth) ===

No child and no arc. The player's loopCounter is set to statsPtr (the ramp's $0E: type $09 = 4, $0B = 5, $11 = 8, $03 = 1) and each loop iteration is StagePlayerMoveXY plus AnimOnce, i.e. one full animation cycle of Y movement at -8 (north, animation $1E, chain $10) or +8 (south, animation $19, chain $0F) per frame. After the loop playerSpeedNs = $FFF8 (north) or $0008 (south), RestorePlayerControl runs and the two step counters are reset as above. LoopEnd decrements before testing, so a count of 0 would run 65536 iterations; the placed ramps never use 0.

=== PLACEMENT ===

58 actor-spawn lines in scene_actors: 26 ramp_east, 22 ramp_west, 6 ramp_north, 4 ramp_south, in scenes 15, 1E, 21, 23, 4F, 53, 82, 83, 85 (Great Wall wall_rampway), 88, A1-A3, A5, A7 (A1, A2 and A5 are in mountain_temple/), B3, B5, CE, CF and D6 (pyramid/). East/west ramps use type 3 except the Itory pair; north uses type 9 (one type 3 in scene 21); south uses type $0B in scene 21 and $11 elsewhere.

=== QUIRKS ===

- The climb labels name the direction of travel: RampClimbNorthStep is the loop head of the NORTH climb and RampClimbSouthStep the loop head of the SOUTH climb; RampPlayerClimbWest is the west entry (ramp_east) and RampPlayerClimbNorth the north entry (ramp_north).
- The launch needs exact equality of the player and ramp coordinates on the axis in stage 2. Whether the player's step size always hits it was not checked at runtime.
- RampPlayerClimbEast stores the exit speed through LDX $06 without checking that SpawnAfter succeeded; if the actor pool were full the climb loop would never end. No evidence that this happens in practice.
- The player's $10 bit $0200 is set here and by slider_glide; its reader is unknown (see OQ-I032-5).

scanline_band_hdma_thinker:
Scanline-band HDMA thinker driven by parallax_scroll_table (Bank 00, 47245-48013). One spawn = one HDMA channel that rewrites a single PPU register per scanline band every frame. Only some table entries scroll a background: others stream COLDATA / CGADSUB / CGDATA colour values or a WH0/WH1 window rectangle through the same band format.

=== SPAWN AND FRAME FLOW ===

thinker-def <#04,#08>: the filter word is $0804, so bit 2 puts it in RunThinkers_Hdma. That pass runs every frame right after ResetHdmaState, so the channel binding is redone every frame. The spawn-record parameter byte (animScratch+2) is the INDEX into parallax_scroll_table (37 word pointers, $00-$24).
1. Entry (once): ParallaxClearBandAccumulators zeroes the 24 band accumulators at $0720-$074F and chatPtr is set to 0.
2. SetEntryHere, then every frame: chatPtr is copied to the global word $0012 and incremented (a frame counter whose bit 0 picks the buffer half), ParallaxBuildHdmaTable rewrites the whole table, and SetupHdmaChannel_Direct binds it to the B-bus register from the entry config (A = register index << 8 | bank $7E, Y = table start). The thinker then leaves $0060 = 1 and $005E = 0.

=== TABLE ENTRY FORMAT (parallax_scroll_table) ===

| Offset | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| +0 word | WRAM buffer address in bank $7E. Even frames build there, odd frames at +$0200 (double buffer: the HDMA channel reads the half written last frame) |
| +2 byte | Bank $7E |
| +3 byte | Config: bits 0-5 = B-bus register index n ($2100 + n; also the index into hdma_channel_config); bit 6 ($40) = camera delta x16; bit 7 ($80) = swap the scroll sources (below) |
| +4 byte | Record size: 4 = constant band, 8 = scroll band, 9 = window rectangle |
| +5 ... | Records, ended by a zero height word (size 4 / 8) or a word with bit 15 set (size 9). An entry that is just $FFFF is unused |

Buffers: $7000, $7400, $7800, $7C00, $8000 and $8400, 1 KB each (two $200 halves). Scenes with two or more parallax thinkers (2B, 2D, 2E, 2F, DF, E0, E3) give them different buffers.

=== SCROLL SOURCES AND STRIDE ===

Default: $18 = bg1ScrollH ($068A, BG1 horizontal scroll) as the multiplicand for proportional bands, and $1C = effectScrollV ($0690, BG2 vertical scroll) as the vertical position that the band heights are measured against. With config bit 7 the sources become $18 = effectScrollH ($068C, BG2 horizontal) and $1C = mapScrollV ($068E, BG1 vertical). $1A = effectDeltaX ($06E4, this frame's camera X delta), shifted left 4 times with config bit 6.
ParallaxResolveEntryStride sets $04 = hdma_entry_stride_by_mode[hdma_channel_config[n] & 7]. That byte is the HDMA ENTRY STRIDE (count byte plus data): 2 for transfer mode 0 (one byte) and 3 for modes 1 and 2 (one word). It is not a speed. The band writers advance the buffer pointer $62 by $04 per entry.

=== RECORD TYPES ===

Size 4 (colour bands): {height word, value word}. The height is a NEGATIVE line count. $1C accumulates the heights; bands whose running sum is still >= 0 lie above the visible area and are skipped. The first band that makes the sum negative starts the table with |sum| lines; later bands use |height|. Each band is written as count byte (at most $7F lines per HDMA entry, longer bands are split) plus the 1 or 2 value bytes. The value word is read from record +2.
Size 8 (scroll bands): {height word, accumulator pointer, factor word, base word}. The accumulator pointer addresses a word in $0720-$0760. Factor <> 0: MulDivide(A = factor, Y = $18) = (factor low byte x $18) / factor high byte, plus base. This is fixed point with 4 fractional bits: factor $0108 is x0.5 and $0110 is x1.0 of the scroll value, $010E is x0.875. Factor = 0: accumulator += base + $1A, an auto-scroll of base/16 pixels per frame that also follows the camera delta. The value stored per HDMA entry is the accumulator >> 4 with the sign extended from bit 11. Bands above the visible area still update their accumulator; bands below the 224-line budget are not processed.
Size 9 (window rectangles, register $2126/$2127 pair WH0/WH1): {x, width, y, height} in map pixels. Each rectangle is converted against bg1ScrollH and mapScrollV into a WH0 (left) / WH1 (right) byte pair. Lines between rectangles get the value $0000. Horizontally a rectangle is skipped when it starts at column $FF or beyond, ends left of the screen, or starts left of the screen and its right edge is at column $FF or beyond; otherwise the right edge is clamped to $FF. Vertically it is skipped when its top is at line $FF or beyond or, if it starts above the screen, when its bottom is at or above line 0 or at line $FF or beyond. The table ends with one more $0000 line.

=== ENTRIES USED BY SCENES ===

Slow horizontal ripple thinker (Bank 00): one sine-wave HDMA table feeding BG1HOFS, started and animated once the scene has finished loading.

slider_glide:
Psycho Slider glide triggers (Bank 00): five trigger actor-defs (SliderGlideTriggerWest, East, North, South and NorthEntry; 29 actor-spawn records in scene_actors, one more through awB2_stair_climb, which JumpFar's to SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain) plus the helpers LockPlayerForClimb, UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and RestorePlayerControl (the last is also called by three ramp exits in ramps.asm).

=== What a trigger detects ===
A trigger runs every frame in its own slot (D = trigger: $14/$16 = its pixel position, $0E = glide length). Y = the player actor. It fires only while Will is Psycho Sliding (RunAttackNS/RunAttackEW in player_character) through its tile: the player's animation index ($28) must be one of the two looping frames of ONE slide direction, and IsPlayerSliderSpriteBank requires the player's sprite bank ($7F0008) to be $8F, the will_alt spriteset that SetPlayerSpriteDirect #04 selects at the start of every slide.
Slide animation indices (will_alt spriteset): south $0C start / $0D loop / $0E finish, north $0F/$10/$11, west $12/$13/$14, east $15/$16/$17 (positive speed = south or east, negative = north or west). The old comments called these 'walk frames' and the bank check a 'walking state'; neither is true.
Each trigger is named for the slide direction it reacts to: SliderGlideTriggerWest = WEST slide ($12/$13, glide X -4 per frame), SliderGlideTriggerEast = EAST slide ($15/$16, X +4), SliderGlideTriggerNorth = NORTH slide ($0F/$10, Y -4), SliderGlideTriggerSouth = SOUTH slide ($0C/$0D, Y +4). The SliderGlideWest/East/North/South routines move the player the same way the slide was already moving.

=== Geometry ===
Slide axis: exact pixel equality with the trigger (X for the West/East triggers, Y for the North/South triggers). Lateral axis: a 32-pixel window, trigger - 7 .. trigger + $18 inclusive (compare is trigger - 8 < player <= trigger - 8 + $20); the old '+/-$20' wording is wrong.

=== The glide ===
On a hit the trigger overwrites the player's entry pointer ($00/$02 of the player actor) with the matching SliderGlide routine and calls LockPlayerForClimb: $0E (the spawn record's type byte >> 1, InitActorFromSceneData mode 1) x 4 is stored as a frame countdown in the PLAYER's statsPtr ($7F0020), the player's velocity words are zeroed, D-pad input is masked (joypadMaskStd $0F00) and playerFlags $0800 is set. The player actor then runs that routine: once, $10 |= $2200 ($2000 = script-driven actor path, $0200 = slide-active flag that RunAttackFlagSetup also sets; its reader is unknown) and $10 bit $0008 (collision-aware movement) is cleared; then every frame the player's X or Y is changed by 4 px directly (no collision test) until the countdown reaches 0: 4 x $0E frames = 16 px per $0E unit (a $0E of 0 would run 65,536 frames). There is no animation during the glide; the slide's looping frame stays on screen.
Landing: clear $2000, stage the FINISH frame of the same slide ($14 west, $17 east, $11 north, $0E south), AnimOnce, then UnlockPlayerAfterClimb. That routine does what RunAttackCleanup does (clear $0200, consume the attack bit in joypadHeld, clear playerFlags $0002) plus clearing climbStateData ($09E0, in fact the ability damage bonus that attack_ability_system sets for the slide), re-enabling collision-aware movement and un-masking joypadMaskStd, then RestorePlayerControl returns the player to PlayerIdleEntry.

db-us/transforms.json (slider_glide) rewrites two vanilla constants: the attack-bit immediate (the vanilla ROM has a different bit, $0080 here after the button remap) and the joypadMaskStd consumption mask (ends in $FC here instead of the vanilla $F0). Comments here describe the post-transform values. Block is marked non-movable because of the tight $& coupling between triggers and climb handlers.
smooth_follow:
Follow/chase movement engine: a small helper actor that steers its spawner toward a target actor (Bank $00; code at $E683 and $EDA8 plus a 544-byte slope table).

Usage: a script starts the helper with COP SpawnAfterMarked at InitFollowAndChase or CopySiblingFollowState, then stores the target actor ID in the new actor's $24 and may preset its animScratch2 (initial facing). The new actor's prev-link ($04) is the spawner, so each step moves both to the same position.

Fields (shared mnemonics, repurposed here): loopCounter ($7F0014) = speed in pixels per frame on the major axis; chatPtr ($7F000A) = base animation ID for the spawner's 16 facings (bit 15 set = leave the spawner's animation and OAM mirror bits alone); animScratch2 ($7F000E) = current facing frame 0-15, clockwise from north ($FFFF = not set yet); orbitAngle ($7F0010) = slope row 0-16 (0 = 45 degrees, 16 = axis-aligned); orbitDiameter ($7F0012) = dither phase 0-15; moveScratch1/2 ($7F002C/2E) = last X/Y step, read back by mu5F_flasher and sEA_solid_arm.

Each aim, FollowChaseMainLoop computes dx = target.X − X and dy = target.Y − 8 − Y, takes absolute values and picks one of 8 octant handlers from the signs and the larger axis (the handler labels name the heading each one produces: ESE, SSE, SSW, WSW, WNW, NNW, NNE, ENE). The handler computes the slope row (ComputeFollowAngle when |dy| dominates, ComputeFollowAngleAlt when |dx| dominates), turns the facing one frame toward the desired one (ResolveFacingFromAxisBase/Alt) and, once aligned, takes a step with ComputeFollowStep: the major axis moves loopCounter pixels and the minor axis moves by the number of 1s in a window of a FollowSlopeDitherTable row (a Bresenham-style dither table, not a sine table).

ApplyFollowMovement adds the step to follower and spawner. The handlers save a resume point with SetEntryHere, so the direction is recomputed (JumpNextFrame to FollowChaseMainLoop) only once the dither phase reaches 8 or more. While the facing is still turning, the actor keeps moving along its current facing (the FollowDirHandler sets the heading and slope; SelectFallbackDirection dispatches it). smooth_follow_child also calls ComputeFollowAngle, ComputeFollowAngleAlt and ComputeFollowStep directly.

Spawned by: InitFollowAndChase from aw_spirit_follower, sg4D_knight_armor, pyDD_queen_spirit_attack, dm_follower_behavior (and an unused initializer); CopySiblingFollowState from mu5F_flasher, sE8_dark_gaia, sEA_solid_arm.
smooth_follow_child:
Straight-line projectile mover (Bank 00, 58587-58964), shared by six enemy projectile scripts. smooth_follow_child is the visible projectile body; a hidden child (SmoothFollowChildTick) aims ONCE at a target actor and then moves along that fixed heading at a fixed speed, copying its position to the body every frame. It does not chase: after the first frame the target is ignored.

=== CALLERS ===

pyCC_blaster (two projectile actors), awB1_wall_walker (code_0BBD19), ec0C_ribber (code_0A843E) and the unused unused_follow_chain set $24 = playerActor, a speed in loopCounter ($7F0014: 1 in pyCC_blaster and ec0C_ribber, 2 in awB1 and gw8A) and then enter smooth_follow_child by a tail call (push of bank and entry minus 1, RTL). gw8A_sand_fanger (code_0B8979) and pyDD_mummy_queen (code_0BA782) skip the body and spawn SmoothFollowChildTick themselves with SpawnAfterMarked (flags $2000), storing playerActor in the child's $24; pyDD uses the speed 4 + $0B02. In every case the spawner is the projectile itself, so the tick moves the spawner.
combat_collision uses SmoothFollowChildDie as the default onCollideCallback: an actor with extendedFlags $0010 and no callback of its own is pointed at it when it touches the player, so these projectiles die after the hit is applied.

=== HOW IT WORKS ===

1. smooth_follow_child clears word $2A, spawns the tick as a hidden marked child (flags $2000) and gives it the target in $24. If the pool is full (Y = $1FC0) it dies at once. Then it plays AnimOnce every frame and dies when its own $10 bit $4000 is set. That bit is the off-screen flag SortActorsByDepth sets when the actor box is completely off the screen; it is not set by a parent. Die also kills the marked tick.
2. On its first frame the tick copies the body's loopCounter (the speed: pixels per frame on the dominant axis), forms dx = target.X - self.X and dy = target.Y - 8 - self.Y, stores |dx| in $0018 and |dy| in $001C (global scratch words, not actor fields) and picks one of 8 handlers from the signs and from which magnitude is larger.
3. The handler calls ComputeFollowAngle (Y-dominant) or ComputeFollowAngleAlt (X-dominant) once. That fills orbitAngle with a slope row of smooth_follow's dither table and clears the dither phase. COP SetEntryHere then saves the address of the next instruction, so every later frame resumes AFTER the aim: ComputeFollowStep gives $0000 = major-axis pixels (loopCounter) and $0002 = minor-axis pixels (0 or 1 per pixel from the slope row), the handler applies them to the tick's own X/Y with its fixed signs, and SmoothFollowWriteParentPos copies X/Y to the body (the tick's $04 prev-link). The heading never changes.

=== HANDLER HEADINGS ===

dx >= 0, dy >= 0 (target south-east): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplySSE (Y += major, X += minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyESE (X += major, Y += minor).
dx >= 0, dy < 0 (north-east): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplyNNE (Y -= major, X += minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyENE (X += major, Y -= minor).
dx < 0, dy >= 0 (south-west): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplySSW (Y += major, X -= minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyWSW (X -= major, Y += minor).
dx < 0, dy < 0 (north-west): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplyNNW (Y -= major, X -= minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyWNW (X -= major, Y -= minor).
Each handler is named after the heading it fires. Five of them were first called SmoothFollowApplyEastPrimary (SSE), EastSecondary (SSW), WestPrimary (WSW), WestSecondary (WNW) and SouthPrimary (NNW), which described neither the dominant axis nor the direction, and three (NNE, ENE, ESE) had only loc_ labels.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said the actor makes a child 'smoothly chase a reference actor', that it updates 'both actors' positions each frame' and that it dies 'when the parent actor sets flag $4000 or on special actor ID $1FC0'. The aim is taken once; only the tick moves and it writes the body's position; $4000 is the body's own off-screen flag and $1FC0 is the pool-exhausted result of the spawn.
SpawnDamageNumberEffect:
Floating damage-number actor (Bank 00, 56500-56579). One spawn is one 16-frame effect: it draws the damage value as digit sprites above the victim and lets them rise one pixel per frame while following the victim's own movement. The old name (SpawnAttackTrailEffect, 'attack trail') and the old text ('ghost copies interpolated between the previous and current position', '16 frames at position then 16 drifting upward', 'when the player or enemies take damage') do not describe it: there is one 16-iteration loop and no ghost copies.

=== SPAWN ===

Two sites in combat_collision: COP SpawnListAppend ( @SpawnDamageNumberEffect, #00, #00, flags ) in PlayerAttackHitTest with flags $2F00, and in ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath with flags $2B00 (that path then ORs $1000 into the child's $12). The fourth operand is the flags word stored into the child's $10, not a priority. Both sites run with the victim as the current actor, so CopyActorState gives the child the victim's X and Y and stores the victim's slot in the child's $24. The caller then writes the packed BCD damage from FormatDamageDigits into the child's $28.
No child is spawned when the victim's $12 bit $0020 (boss) is set or when the damage is 1000 or more (FormatDamageDigits returns carry). No other spawn site exists in extracted/.

=== BODY ===

1. $0E := $3200: the attribute word ORed into every digit tile (OAM high byte $32 = priority 3, palette 1).
2. $16 -= $10: start 16 pixels above the victim.
3. Y := $24 (the victim); remember its X and Y in $20 and $22.
4. 16 iterations (LoopStart #10 = 16): add the victim's X movement since last frame to $14, add its Y movement minus 1 to $16 (so the digits rise one pixel per frame), refresh $20/$22, copy $28 to the absolute scratch word $0000 and call ComposeDigitSprites. ComposeDigitSprites puts the first digit at $14 - 12 and appends one 6-byte entry per digit to the compose buffer at $7F3100. LoopEnd yields every iteration, so the digits are re-emitted every frame; then Die.

The scratch word is written with the absolute address $0000 on purpose: it is not the actor's own $00/$01 re-entry address.

=== HAZARD ===

The loop re-reads the victim's position through $24 every frame and never checks that the slot still holds the same actor. If the victim died and its slot were reused within the 16 frames, the number would follow whatever occupies the slot (analysis only, not run; OQ-I041-5).

DamageNumberShort_unused is an unreferenced variant of this routine.

Flags $0302: bit $0200 is part of the combat_collision skip masks (OQ-I030-2); $0100 and $0002 are undecoded.

SpawnFieldRevealEffect:
Room-reveal effect (Bank 00, 56818-57107): after the enemy that guards a hidden room part is defeated, a glowing sprite rises from the corpse, flies to the centre of the revealed region, flashes, scatters ten sparkles and swaps the background tiles (StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx + ApplyBgChange). Three actor bodies live in this file: SpawnFieldRevealEffect, field_reveal_scatter (which falls through into field_reveal_flash) and field_reveal_flash.

=== SPAWN ===

SpawnListAppend ( SpawnFieldRevealEffect, #00, #00, #$0342 ) in StandardEnemyDefeatHandler (56375), EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill (697548), pyCC_mystic_ball (771970) and awB1_wall_walker (770414). The spawner copies its deathActionIdx ($7F0024, the event-block index of its scene record) into the child; EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill guards the spawn with event flag $0100 + index so each reveal fires once.

=== TARGET ===

event_block_table is indexed by deathActionIdx x 8. The bytes used are +3 width, +4 height, +5 dstX and +6 dstY (event-block-def, tile units). The flight target is the centre of the destination rectangle in pixels: moveXAlt = (2 x dstX + width) x 8, moveYAlt = (2 x dstY + height) x 8. orbitAngle := width / 2 and orbitDiameter := height / 2 are passed to the scatter particles as their range tier.

=== SEQUENCE ===

Flags $0342, palette 0, anim $29: three rising passes (Y chains $02, $12, $14), a two-pass hover loop, sprite priority $30, then StageMove to the target at 4 px per frame (TickMove). On arrival: a field_reveal_flash child, a 2-tick wait (WaitByte #01), $10 |= $2000, then ten field_reveal_scatter children (one every 5 ticks: WaitByte #03 is 4 ticks and LoopEnd yields once more; each gets the half-width and half-height), then StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx (SFX $0F on both channels, stages the swap), ApplyBgChange and Die. Each child gets $12 |= $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, which CopyActorState clears).

The old header named an 'Incan Ruins wind trap' as a user (the four callers above are the real ones) and called +3 / +5 the 'target X tile' and 'X size'; they are the width and dstX.
SpawnItemSparkleEffect:
Item-effect sparkle actor (Bank 00, 56579-56667). One spawn is a 24-frame effect that draws two small tiles side by side at the actor's position: 8 frames standing still, then 16 frames rising one pixel per frame. The old text ('four tile entries flanking the hit position', 'spawned during inventory-screen hit feedback') is wrong: it writes two compose-buffer entries per frame and its only spawn site is GiveItemToPlayer.

=== SPAWN ===

inventory_mgmt.GiveItemToPlayer, special-item branch: effect index >= 6 (item id $86 and up) adds 5 to hpToHeal, runs COP SpawnListAppend ( @SpawnItemSparkleEffect, #00, #00, #$2F00 ) after PHD / TXA / TCD, then plays sound #22. The fourth operand is the flags word for the child's $10. The child copies position from the actor whose slot is in X when the item is given (the in-line comment there says the player; not verified). No item id of $86 or more was found in the chest tables or GiveItem operands of extracted/, so whether this path is reachable in the shipped game is open (OQ-I042-1).

=== BODY ===

SpawnItemSparkleEffect: LoopStart #08 (8 frames) calling AppendSparkleOamEntries, then LoopStart #10 (16 frames) that first subtracts 1 from $16 and then calls it again; LoopEnd yields every iteration; then Die. There is no initial Y offset (unlike the damage numbers).
AppendSparkleOamEntries writes two 6-byte entries at the compose-buffer cursor oamWriteOffset ($00D8) in the buffer at $7F3100: X - 4 with tile word $327A, and X + 4 with tile word $327B, both at Y = $16. The tile words are tile $7A and $7B with attribute $3200 (the same priority 3 / palette 1 as the damage digits; tiles $70-$79 are the digits). The cursor advances by $0C. No terminator is written here; the main loop writes $FF after all actors have run.

What tiles $7A / $7B look like was not checked (OQ-I042-2).

StandardEnemyDefeatHandler:
Standard field-enemy defeat script (Bank 00, 56202-56816). The defeated actor itself runs it (X = D = the victim). Entered in three ways: (1) as the default death script: hit_stagger_controller (HitStaggerResolveHit) and two inline paths in combat_collision set the victim's entry point to StandardEnemyDefeatHandler when its HP reaches zero and it has no onDeathCallback ($7F1004); (2) by COP JumpFar from the own scripts of 13 enemies (pyCC_mystic_ball, pyD2_haunt, awB1_wall_walker, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw83_asp, mu67_vampires, av6E_draco, sg55_viper, sg4D_dynapede, sg4E_nitropede, sg4D_cyber, ir29_castoth, sg51_statue) and from EnemyDefeatDispatch (the last enemy of a scene); (3) ir20_statue and ir26_statue JumpFar straight into EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop.

=== FLOW ===

1. Kill counters (StandardEnemyDefeatHandler). Skipped when statsPtr points at the first enemy_stats_table entry (an EnemyInitBasic actor: HP 1, no stats) or extendedFlags bit $0080 (the boss bit). Otherwise enemiesRemainingBcd ($0AEE) -= 1 in decimal mode, enemiesRemaining ($0AEC) -= 1 in hex, and the new count is also kept in orbitAngle ($7F0010,X): 0 means this was the last enemy on the map.
2. Flash (EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop). Movement is halted ($2C / $2E and moveScratch1 / 2 := 0), SFX #06 plays on channel 1 and EnemyDeathFlash is spawned at the enemy (flags $0302; bit $0002 draws it in front of every actor). The flash gets $12 bit $1000 (CopyActorState clears it) so that it keeps running in display-filter actor mode, then WaitByte 2.
3. No-stats and boss actors go to EnemyDefeatBossCleanup: hide ($10 |= $2000), ClearSolidHere if extendedFlags $0008, WaitByte 5, Die. They get no kill flag, gem drop or reward.
4. Other enemies: SetDungeonKillFlag (the enemyNum bit in wramFlags, so the enemy stays dead on re-entry), then the gem decision, hide ($10 |= $2000), ClearSolidHere if extendedFlags $0008, the field reveal, and finally Die when enemies remain or EnemyStatBonusReward when this was the last one.
   Gem decision: TestFlag_0300 (event flag $0300 + scene = this scene's clear reward was already claimed) set, or orbitAngle nonzero (enemies remain): drop a gem when the stats byte +3 (gemDropType) is nonzero, through EnemyGemDropRouter. Last enemy with the reward still unclaimed: no gem, the stat reward replaces it.
   Field reveal: deathActionIdx ($7F0024,X) nonzero and event flag $0100 + idx still clear: set it and spawn SpawnFieldRevealEffect (flags $0342, with $12 $1000), handing it the index.
5. EnemyStatBonusReward (last enemy only): enemy_clear_reward_table[scene] selects the pickup (0 none, 1 HP, 2 STR, 3 or more DEF) unless the scene flag $0300 is already set. It sets displayModeFlags $0080 (display-filter actor mode: only actors with $12 $1000 run, so the world freezes while the pickup plays), spawns reward_actors.e_hp_increase / e_str_increase / e_def_increase (flags $1000, $12 $1000) and Dies. RewardActorVFX sets the scene flag later (see reward_actors).

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said ComposeDigitSprites_AtCursor assigns this as the OnDeath callback during enemy setup (no code there references it; the engine falls back to it when $7F1004 is empty), that it is about 360 bytes (it spans about 614), that it calls ClearLowHere (the COP is ClearSolidHere) and that the $12 $1000 write is a 'priority boost'. The comment on the first block said the gem drop is skipped when scene flag $0300 is set; it is the opposite: gems drop when the flag is set or enemies remain. EnemyDropSystem.asm repeated the inverted condition (corrected there). The 'about 20 enemy actor scripts' were 13 JumpFar sites, EnemyDefeatDispatch, 2 statues and 3 engine sites.
statue_inventory_reward:
Mystic-statue reward ceremony (scene $FD, Bank 00, 52569-53033). Six copies of this actor spawn in scene $FD, one per pedestal; only the copy whose table index equals globalScriptIndex ($0AAC) runs the ceremony, the others stay hidden or show a statue that was collected before. Scene $FD lists nothing but these six actors (no player, no camera).

=== TRIGGER ===
Six scripts queue scene $FD with COP QueueMapChange: index 0 gs2E_crew2 (Gold Ship), 1 sg55_mystic_statue (Viper), 2 mu66_rama_spirits (Mu), 3 gw8A_sand_fanger (Great Wall), 4 pyDD_mystic_statue (Mummy Queen), 5 btDE_olman (Babel). Each first writes globalScriptIndex = its index, sourceSceneId ($0B12) = its own scene ($2E, $55, $66, $8A, $CD, $DE) and the return position in $0B08-$0B10 (tile X, tile Y, scroll parameters).

=== TABLE statue_reward_table ===
6 entries of 4 bytes (3 fields + 1 tail byte, never read by the two actors):
| Index | Flag | Sprite | Match | Boss / event | Trigger script |
|-------|------|--------|-------|--------------|----------------|
| 0 | $F8 | $3A | $00 | Gold Ship event | gs2E_crew2.asm |
| 1 | $F9 | $3B | $01 | Viper | sg55_mystic_statue.asm |
| 2 | $FA | $3C | $02 | Mu (Rama's spirits) | mu66_rama_spirits.asm |
| 3 | $FB | $3D | $03 | Sand Fanger | gw8A_sand_fanger.asm |
| 4 | $FC | $3E | $04 | Mummy Queen | pyDD_mystic_statue.asm |
| 5 | $FD | $3F | $05 | Olman (Babel) | btDE_olman.asm |
Flag = event flag index: flag N is bit (N AND 7) of byte $0A00 + N / 8, so $F8-$FD are bits 0-5 of the single byte $0A1F. Sprite = animation index ($28) in inventory_spritemap. Match = the globalScriptIndex value for which this entry is the statue being awarded (it equals the row number).

=== ACTOR FLOW ===
1. Entry: joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button hidden; this build's value, the vanilla $FFF0 is rewritten by transforms.json, probably to cover the remapped X bit $0004), NudgePosition(8, 8) plus (0, -8) when bit 4 of the spawn parameter is set (same record encoding and positions as inventory_statue_slot), metasprite inventory_spritemap. Initial flags $3000: hidden, and running in the display-filtered pass.
2. Screen setup by direct register writes: BG1 tilemap at VRAM word $0800 (BG1SC $08), BG2 tilemap at $0C00 (BG2SC $0C), main screen BG1 + BG2 + OBJ (TM $13), sub screen BG1 + OBJ (TS $11), colour math with the sub screen as the source (CGWSEL $82) added onto BG2 only (CGADSUB $02). There is no BGMODE write. srcCacheBgD+1 ($0676-$0677) is cleared to invalidate graphics cache slot D.
3. Every copy: index = low nibble of the parameter. TestFlagRaw(flag): set -> StatueRewardAlreadyClaimed (statue shown, idle). Otherwise match against globalScriptIndex: different -> StatueRewardNotThisStatue (stays hidden, idle).
4. The matching copy: SetFlagRaw (statue collected for good; inventory_statue_slot shows it from now on), animation frame set (still hidden), then 8 StatueRewardOrbitalSparkle actors with start angles $21, $41, ... $E1, $0101 (the loop ends when the angle word reaches $0101; only the low byte is an angle, so they are $20 apart).
5. Waiting: globalScriptIndex becomes a 180-frame countdown. Each frame it is decremented; at zero the ceremony jumps straight to step 7 (no confetti). While IsMusicPlaying (SPC transfer pending or the display-filter bit set) it waits. When that ends the counter is zeroed, WaitByte $0F, sound $2525 on both channels, then the orbitDiameter of the LAST sparkle spawned is polled each frame until it is 0.
6. Reveal: the hidden bit is cleared and 60 StatueRewardConfettiBurst actors are spawned, one per frame (LoopEnd yields every iteration). Each burst tests frameCounter AND 3 on its first tick and dies at once unless that is 0, so only about one burst in four is visible.
7. Exit: sceneNext = sourceSceneId (a nonzero sceneNext starts the scene change), warpDestX / warpDestY = $0B08 / $0B0C x 16, warpFacing = 3, warpScrollParams = $0B10, gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 (exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade) and gfxCacheIdxB = $0303 (speed 3 for both).
StopPlayerOnDeath:
Helper called once by CheckPlayerDeath (combat_collision) when playerHp reaches zero (Bank 00, RTL). Y = the player actor's address (CheckPlayerDeath loads it with LDY playerActor) and A is 16 bits wide.

CheckPlayerDeath has already set playerFlags $0200 (game over) and replaced the player actor's entry point ($00/$02) with GameOverSequence before it calls this routine. This routine then zeroes playerSpeedEw and playerSpeedNs (the player stops moving), zeroes the actor's $08 (the wait counter that the actor runner decrements before running a script, so a pending hold time cannot delay GameOverSequence) and ORs $0200 into the player actor's own flag word $10.

Two different $0200 bits: playerFlags $0200 = game over, set by the caller before this call (it is what CheckPlayerDeath and GlobalInputHandler test); bit $0200 of the actor's $10, set here, is a different bit. No code that reads the actor bit was found (the Psycho Slider sets and clears the same bit), so the old claim that it "freezes movement" is unverified. docs/wram-memory-map.md lists "$0200 deathFlag, set by StopPlayerOnDeath" as a WRAM address; that entry confuses a bit mask with an address.
system_core:
Core system loop and CPU interrupt vectors.

Contains the SNES reset vector (emulation → native mode switch), the COP/NMI/IRQ vectors, the hardware initialization and boot sequence (SystemInit), and the main game loop that runs the per-frame subsystems: VBlank sync, scene management, actor processing, sprite composition, camera scrolling, HUD update and the music-upload hook.

Also provides three context-specific frame update variants (all re-entrant, callable from COP handlers and from the NMI):
- UpdateFrameDialogue: lightweight update during text/dialogue display
- UpdateFrameRender: render-only update (sprite sort/compose, HDMA reset, HUD, cutscene thinkers) for menus and transitions
- UpdateFrameFull: complete subsystem tick run from inside the NMI handler while the main loop is blocked in a music upload (musicTransitionState > 0)

The NMI handler manages VRAM DMA (scroll registers, dirty tilemap strips, CGRAM, OAM, the partial BG3 upload, then either the player tiles or the normal queued writes), reads the joypad auto-read result and sends the queued SFX byte to the SPC.

UpdateHUD runs the heads-up display: HP recovery animation (every 8th frame), stat dirty-checking (HP, max HP, gems) with a BG3 redraw, and the enemy health bar timer (a 60-frame hold, then the bar is cleared; the 25- and 30-frame values stored along the way are overwritten at once). UpdateFrameCounters maintains the invincibility timer and the capped global frame timer.

Utility routines: scroll register upload with layer priority support and the one-shot VRAM DMA (ExecuteVramDma). OamFillE0_unused/OamFillConstant_unused (an OAM fill) have no caller in extracted/.
town_door:
Reusable town door (Bank 00, 50675-50732). 16 placements in three scenes: $01 South Cape (5 doors), $32 Freejia (4) and $91 (7); fr32_guide spawns one more at runtime (SpawnAfterAbsFlags at TownDoorInit, X $0278, Y $0230). The old docs say '16 scenes'.

A door is drawn closed (frame #01 of spriteset_npc_props) and solid. When the player is next to it (BranchIfPlayerNear radius 1: both |dx| and |dy| within 16 px) and HOLDS UP (joypad $0800) for 8 consecutive frames, it plays SFX #0E on channel 2, clears its solid mark, switches to the open frame #00 and idles for the rest of the scene visit (nothing closes it again). The old header said 'A-button press'; the code tests the Up direction. Releasing Up or leaving the box restarts the count: the loop is re-entered through TownDoorProximityCheck and LoopStart reloads the counter.

A door that is already within radius 1 when it spawns skips the closed state: TownDoorInit branches straight to TownDoorOpenIdle, so it starts open (the player has just come out of the building).

Re-entry: after the first off-screen wait the entry pointer ($00) is the WaitWhileOffscreen op itself (it stores itself while the door is off-screen, which is the state at spawn because InitActorFromSceneData sets Flags10 bit $4000). Every later frame resumes there, passes straight through while on-screen and runs TownDoorProximityCheck. A door that is already on-screen at its first pass would instead be re-entered at AnimOnce and run the Init-time BranchIfPlayerNear to TownDoorOpenIdle first, which would open it without the Up hold; not verified at runtime (OQ-I043-1).

The solid mark: MarkSolidHere / ClearSolidHere OR and AND the high nibble of the collision cells under the actor's hitbox rectangle, not a single tile. The door itself is not a warp; the building entrance is a separate trigger.
